Evaluating behavioural responses of macropods to drones
abstractText: Context Wildlife monitoring is a crucial component of conservation management, and drones are an increasingly important tool for wildlife surveys. The response of wildlife to drone activities can vary depending on various factors, hence, the development of site- and species-specific protocols for drone-survey methods should be prioritised. Aims In this study, we aimed to evaluate the behavioural responses of two large terrestrial mammals from Tasmania, Australia – Bennett’s wallaby (Notamacropus rufogriseus) and Forester kangaroo (Macropus giganteus tasmaniensis) – towards a drone, with the goal of determining the feasibility of deploying drones for population monitoring of these species in their natural habitats. Methods We investigated the impacts of drone presence on Bennett’s wallaby and Forester kangaroo using a commercial quadcopter model. Individuals were observed under controlled drone approaches conducted at six flight altitudes, and behavioural responses were classified as undisturbed, vigilant or fled based on direct observation and video analysis. Key results We found that both macropod species showed increasing behavioural responses to the drone, including evasion, at lower flight altitudes and higher drone noise levels, particularly at 40 m above ground level (AGL) and below. At lower sound levels (48 dB and below, corresponding to flight altitudes above 50 m AGL), animals’ responses were minimal. These results indicate that drone-based surveys of Forester kangaroos and Bennett’s wallabies can be conducted with minimal disturbance when appropriate operational parameters are applied. Conclusions Our findings support the adoption of flight altitudes of 40–60 m AGL as a general guideline for reducing behavioural disturbance during drone-based monitoring of macropods under conditions similar to those examined in this study. These findings highlight the potential for drone-based monitoring of macropods with minimal behavioural disturbance when appropriate flight parameters are applied. Implications Our study has established fundamental information on the behavioural responses of Forester kangaroos and Bennett’s wallabies to drone operations, helping to identify flight parameters that can minimise disturbance during wildlife surveys. These findings can inform the development of drone-based monitoring protocols for macropods in Tasmania and provide a basis for further evaluation of species-specific responses to drone operations.

title: Quantifying structural variants in chromosomes using landmark-based disparity
abstractText: Abstract Background Chromosomal architecture has played a key role in the evolution of biodiversity. Detecting structural variants (SVs) on chromosomes has informed the study of speciation, sex determination, adaptation, and some of the earliest divergences in the tree of life. Here we present a computationally non-intensive approach based on geometric morphometrics, that uses coordinate data from conserved, single-copy DNA sequences as landmarks to quantify structural disparities of focal chromosomes via primary or haploid genome assemblies across multiple species, individuals, or cell types. Results Based on two approaches, we show that this ‘geno-metric’ method can be applied at micro- and macroevolutionary scales to discover and diagnose SVs. Using human X-linked single-copy genes and ultraconserved elements as genomic ‘landmarks’, we provide empirical demonstrations with amniote sex chromosomes, the Drosophila virilis group, and placental mammal genomes. Landmark-based structural disparity analysis effectively identifies chromosomal SVs and has parallels with traditional morphometrics regarding chromosome size, landmark orientation and landmark availability. Using simulations, we show that structural disparity inferred from ultraconserved elements is correlated with overall levels of chromosome evolution; an attribute which is consistent with observed disparity between and within mammalian orders. We found that the disparity patterns of SVs have significant phylogenetic signal, giving them broad importance for studying evolutionary biology. We also discuss alternative approaches that may be used to extract genomic coordinates and SV data for multi-species comparisons. Conclusions Structural disparity analysis is a reference free, whole-genome alignment free, non-pairwise comparative method that uses coordinates of single-copy genomic markers and dimensionality reduction methods to measure SVs on homologous chromosome sets. The method offers an intuitive, rapid mechanism to detect and measure SVs and consequently, offers the potential to reveal broader patterns of chromosome evolution related to expansions, contractions, rearrangements and phylogenetic history.

title: Enhancing FMCW radar accuracy for adaptive cruise control using CFAR algorithms in adverse weather
abstractText: Abstract Adaptive cruise control (ACC) relies on accurate range and relative-velocity measurements of the preceding vehicle, which frequency-modulated continuous-wave (FMCW) radar provides. Under adverse conditions, however, clutter from rain, fog, and insect swarms degrades these measurements. This study presents a 77 GHz FMCW radar framework for ACC that integrates physically motivated models of rain, fog, and insect clutter with a two-dimensional cell-averaging constant false alarm rate (CA-CFAR) detector. By adapting its threshold to the local clutter level, the detector suppresses clutter-induced peaks and enables more reliable identification of the target response. Simulations up to 200 m show that all three clutter types increase the estimation errors with clutter intensity and distance, and that CFAR processing consistently reduces them. At 83 m under 25 mm/h rain, the range error decreases from 0.50 m to 0.24 m; at 63 m, the velocity error decreases from 4.7% to 2.3%; and at 200 m in dense fog, the range error decreases from 11.25% to 6.20%. The framework detects three targets up to 200 m and resolves velocities as low as 0.0083 m/s, supporting reliable ACC operation in adverse weather.

title: Evaluating LLMs on Italian through multi-prompt: the Evalita-LLM benchmark
abstractText: Abstract We present Evalita-LLM, a novel benchmark designed to evaluate Large Language Models (LLMs) on Italian tasks. The key innovation of Evalita-LLM is the use of multiple prompts for each task, which mitigates the model’s sensitivity to specific prompt formulations and ensures a robust and objective performance assessment. We propose an iterative methodology for selecting and validating multiple prompts, and metrics that capture both high performance and stability of a prompt given a set of LLMs. The resulting Evalita-LLM multi-prompt benchmark is based on ten native Italian tasks, eliminating translation issues and potential cultural biases. It includes a mix of multiple-choice and generative tasks, enabling more natural interactions with LLMs. We report experimental results from the benchmark’s development phase, along with performance statistics for several state-of-the-art LLMs. Evalita-LLM is publicly available with a leaderboard hosted on Hugging Face to support transparent evaluation and comparison of LLMs.

title: Future projections of distribution dynamics and biomass of dwarf bamboos in northern Japan using a dynamic global vegetation model
abstractText: Abstract Dwarf bamboo (DB) species are widespread across East Asia, including northern Japan, where they form pure communities and strongly influence ecosystem structure and vegetation dynamics, including tree regeneration. The regional distribution of different DB types is strongly associated with maximum snow depth, which is expected to decrease under future warming. Climate-induced changes in snow conditions may therefore alter both the distribution and biomass of DB vegetation. However, dwarf bamboo and its sensitivity to snow conditions have rarely been represented in vegetation models, such as dynamic global vegetation models, which limits our ability to project the effect and change of DB under climate change. In this study, we developed a dwarf bamboo submodule within the SEIB-DGVM framework to simulate future changes in the distribution and aboveground biomass (AGB) of DB species in Hokkaido, northern Japan. Under the RCP8.5 scenario, our simulations indicate that Sasa nipponica , a smaller species adapted to shallower snow conditions, is likely to expand its distribution. Across three different climate datasets under the RCP8.5 scenario, an average of 72.8% of the grid cells classified as the tall-stature type under the present-day climate were projected to shift to the short-stature type. Simulated AGB responses differed depending on whether the dominant DB type remained stable or shifted between types. Across all grid cells, mean AGB decreased by 403 g DM m⁻ 2 , corresponding to approximately 16.1% decrease relative to the current climate. Our results demonstrate that climate-driven reductions in snow depth can cause substantial shifts in the distribution and biomass of dwarf bamboo. Explicitly representing these snow-mediated vegetation shifts in DGVMs may therefore improve projections of non-tree vegetation dynamics under climate change. The developed model provides a framework for evaluating future changes in dwarf bamboo vegetation and their ecological consequences in northern Japan.

title: Quantum neural networks for wind power prediction: a benchmark against classical machine learning models
abstractText: Abstract Quantum Machine Learning (QML) is an emerging field at the intersection of quantum computing and machine learning that aims to enhance classical learning methods by leveraging principles such as superposition and entanglement. However, skepticism remains regarding its practical advantages, particularly due to the limitations of noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) devices. This study addresses these concerns through a systematic evaluation of Quantum Neural Networks (QNNs), quantum-inspired counterparts of Artificial Neural Networks (ANNs). We construct and analyze 12 distinct QNN configurations by combining two quantum feature maps with six entanglement strategies for ansatz design. Experiments conducted on a wind energy dataset show that QNNs can achieve competitive or superior performance compared to classical baseline models, with the best-performing configuration (QNN-3) reaching an R 2 score of up to 0.94 when forecasting wind power output using four input features. In addition, we provide a detailed analysis of simulation time across different configurations, highlighting trade-offs between model complexity and computational cost. These findings demonstrate the potential of QNNs as viable models for predictive tasks and contribute to the ongoing evaluation of QML in real-world applications.

title: CurvEdgeNet: edge feature integration with Ricci curvature for circRNA-disease association prediction
abstractText: Circular RNAs (circRNAs) are crucial regulators in disease pathogenesis, making accurate circRNA-disease association prediction essential for understanding disease mechanisms and therapeutic development. Current computational methods rely on simple network topologies and linear feature extraction, failing to capture the non-Euclidean geometric properties and complex interaction patterns in biological networks, which significantly impairs prediction accuracy and biological interpretability. To address this challenge, we propose CurvEdgeNet, a novel heterogeneous graph neural network framework that integrates discrete curvature and edge-enhancement mechanisms. CurvEdgeNet employs a multi-stage architecture: first constructing a heterogeneous network using multiple similarity measures and known associations, then designing a curvature-enhanced graph attention network that introduces Ollivier-Ricci curvature from discrete geometry into circRNA-disease prediction, embedding geometric edge properties into graph neural network message-passing to effectively capture local topological features, while global feature dependencies are captured through a BiLSTM module, and finally fusing these complementary features using multi-head attention before feeding them into a multilayer perceptron for prediction. Five-fold cross-validation on three independent datasets—CircR2Disease V2, CircRNA2Disease V2, and CircFunBase—demonstrates excellent predictive performance, achieving AUC values of 0.9854±0.0031, 0.9900±0.0020, and 0.9932±0.0016 respectively. This geometry-enhanced approach provides new insights into biological networks' non-Euclidean properties and offers a powerful tool for discovering potential circRNA-disease associations, facilitating biomarker identification and therapeutic target development.

title: Complexity-informed causal modeling of neurodevelopmental trajectories in pediatric high-grade gliomas: divergences from neural stem cell signatures
abstractText: Abstract Pediatric high-grade gliomas (pHGGs) are lethal evolutionary disorders with stalled developmental pathways and disturbed differentiation hierarchies. We integrate transcriptional and algorithmic network complexity-based perturbation analysis to elucidate gene expression patterns and molecular divergence between Diffuse Midline Gliomas (DMG; previously DIPG) and glioblastoma (GBM), revealing shared developmental programs steering cell fate decision-making. Our complex systems approach supports the emerging paradigm that pHGGs are neurodevelopmental disorders with hybrid lineage identities and disrupted patterning. We identify dysregulated neurodevelopmental and morphogenetic signatures, alongside bioelectric and neurotransmitter signaling programs that alter synaptic organization, neuronal fate commitment, and phenotypic plasticity, regulating glioma phenotypic switching (cell state-transitions). In silico candidate transition-associated network signatures and regulators of plasticity were predicted as possible predictive biomarkers and therapeutic targets, reinforcing the view that pediatric gliomas are disorders of cell fate decisions and collective cellular identity. Neuronal and synaptic enrichment is interpreted as a candidate neurodevelopmental network program emerging from disrupted cell fate decision-making. Across validation cohorts, these predictive signatures localized to progenitor-like, NPC/OPC-like, hybrid/ambiguous, immune, and extracellular matrix-associated compartments, supporting recurrence-associated plasticity dynamics. Decoded cell fate transition-associated signatures indicate recurrence-associated remodeling of neural progenitor, OPC-like, neurosynaptic interface, immune, and matrisome-associated programs, as computationally inferred network features. Using graph network-based complexity signatures, our algorithms identified candidate network-associated plasticity markers and interpretable regulatory drivers underlying latent glioma cell fate dynamics. These computational findings may help advance ‘differentiation therapy’ as a systems medicine strategy, discovering plasticity regulators to reprogram malignant fates toward stable lineages, offering complex systems-based targets for cancer reversion and predictive, preventive, and precision oncology.

title: Generation of spatiotemporal optical coil with controllable transverse intensity chirality
abstractText: Abstract Chirality is a fundamental asymmetry in nature. In optics, control of chirality is evolving from spatial properties like polarization to the temporal chirality of local fields. Conventional approaches, however, encode chirality in abstract degrees of freedom such as phase or polarization, limiting direct and efficient coupling with matter on ultrafast timescales. We introduce and experimentally demonstrate a paradigm of intensity-driven optical chirality, where handedness is physically inscribed into the trajectory of spatiotemporal energy flow. Through the engineered non-collinear collision of Spatiotemporal Optical Vortices, the Spatiotemporal Optical Coil is generated. The coil’s chirality manifests as a physical torsion of its volumetric energy flow, a property fundamentally independent of phase and polarization. By employing femtosecond tomography and phase-resolved reconstruction, we map the complete three-dimensional spatiotemporal intensity field, directly observing the evolution of singularity lines. This approach reveals programmable scaling relations between the coil’s topology and interaction geometry, extending the concept of chirality to the energy-flow level. The introduced volumetric chiral density directly correlates with the optical forces and torques exerted on chiral particles, establishing a new, intensity-driven degree of freedom for topological photonics and enabling novel schemes for ultrafast chiral-selective excitation and high-dimensional information encoding.

title: Community benchmarking of generative models for privacy-preserving synthetic bulk RNA-seq data generation
abstractText: Abstract Background The synthesis of anonymized data derived from real-world cohorts offers a promising strategy for regulatory-compliant and privacy-preserving biological data sharing, potentially facilitating model development that can improve predictive performance. However, the extent to which generative models can preserve biological signals while remaining resilient to adversarial privacy attacks in high-dimensional omics contexts remains underexplored. To address this gap, the CAMDA 2025 Health Privacy Challenge launched a community-driven effort to systematically benchmark synthetic and privacy-preserving data generation for bulk RNA-seq cohorts. Results Building on this initiative, we systematically benchmarked 11 generative methods across two cancer cohorts (∼1,000 and ∼5,000 patients) over 978 landmark genes. Methods were evaluated across complementary axes of distributional fidelity, downstream utility, biological plausibility and empirical privacy risk, with emphasis on trade-offs between vulnerability to membership inference attacks (MIA) and other evaluation dimensions. Expressive deep generative models achieved strong predictive utility and differential expression recovery, but were often more vulnerable to membership inference risk. Differentially private methods improved resistance to attacks at the cost of reduced utility, while simpler statistical approaches offered competitive utility with moderate privacy risk and fast training. Conclusions Synthetic bulk RNA-seq quality is inherently multi-dimensional and shaped by trade-offs between utility, biological preservation and privacy. Our results indicate that differences in model architecture drive distinct trade-offs across these axes, suggesting that model choice should align with dataset characteristics, intended downstream use and privacy requirements. Privacy risk should also be assessed using multiple complementary attack methods and, where possible, formal differential privacy protection.

title: Incidence, timing, refractive patterns, and management of enhancement after keratorefractive lenticule extraction (KLEx): A 3,396-eye single-center registry study
abstractText: Abstract Background The literature on enhancement after keratorefractive lenticule extraction (KLEx) remains limited, particularly when retreatment frequency is anchored to a large real-world denominator. The purpose of this study was to evaluate the incidence, timing, refractive patterns, and management of secondary enhancement after KLEx in a large single-center clinical registry and to examine whether a revised treatment nomogram introduced on July 1, 2024 was associated with lower subsequent enhancement frequency. Methods A retrospective registry study was performed at Eye Clinic Svjetlost, Zagreb, Croatia. The denominator registry comprised 3,396 KLEx eyes treated on the SCHWIND ATOS platform. Enhancement eyes were identified from dedicated cap-to-flap and transepithelial photorefractive keratectomy (TransPRK) workbooks. Main outcomes were enhancement rate, time to enhancement, pre-enhancement refractive characteristics, technique distribution, observed postoperative uncorrected distance visual acuity (UDVA), and paired ocular and corneal wavefront outcomes. Because postoperative corrected distance visual acuity (CDVA) was not systematically captured, an exploratory surrogate CDVA analysis was performed using pre-enhancement CDVA and observed postoperative UDVA; the safety index derived from this analysis represents an upper-bound estimate. Exact era denominators were 1,198 eyes before July 1, 2024 and 2,198 eyes on or after July 1, 2024. Results A total of 61 eyes of 48 patients underwent enhancement, corresponding to an overall enhancement rate of 1.80% (61/3,396; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.38% to 2.30%). Median time to enhancement was 4.1 months (interquartile range [IQR], 2.7 to 5.5 months; range, 1.1 to 51.0 months), and 47 of 61 eyes (77.0%) were enhanced within 6 months. Mean pre-enhancement spherical equivalent (SEQ) was − 0.80 ± 0.72 D (range, − 2.25 to 1.00 D). Forty eyes underwent cap-to-flap conversion and 21 underwent TransPRK. Cap-to-flap conversion was technically successful in 39 of 40 eyes (97.5%). In harmonized analyses, mean observed UDVA improved from 0.18 ± 0.18 to − 0.03 ± 0.10 logMAR at 1 month (n = 41, P < .001) and from 0.15 ± 0.12 to − 0.05 ± 0.08 logMAR at 3 months (n = 20, P < .001). Ocular wavefront metrics remained stable. Corneal trefoil at 6 mm increased modestly from 0.18 ± 0.09 to 0.22 ± 0.13 µm (n = 58, P = .035) without correlation to latest observed UDVA. Era analysis showed 46 enhancements among 1,198 eyes treated before July 1, 2024 (3.84%) versus 15 among 2,198 eyes treated thereafter (0.68%), corresponding to an 82.2% relative reduction (χ² = 43.82, P < .001; risk ratio for post- versus pre-nomogram enhancement frequency, 0.18, 95% CI 0.10 to 0.32). Conclusions Secondary enhancement after KLEx was uncommon in this 3,396-eye registry and usually occurred early after primary surgery. A revised age-adjusted nomogram introduced on July 1, 2024 was associated with a markedly lower enhancement frequency in the subsequent era. Cap-to-flap conversion and TransPRK were both viable enhancement strategies in routine practice, but the principal contribution of this study is denominator-anchored reporting of enhancement incidence, timing, and workflow rather than proof of optical superiority between enhancement techniques.

title: Reformer pilates improves posture and functional movement: a randomised comparison of AI-assisted and traditional personalisation
abstractText: This study compared the effects of a traditional fixed Reformer Pilates programme and a ChatGPT-assisted, weekly-adapted Reformer Pilates programme on postural alignment and functional movement quality in healthy adults. Thirty volunteers aged 20–45 years with a minimum of 6 months of prior Pilates experience were randomly allocated to an AI-assisted group (n=15) or a traditional group (n=15). Both groups trained on the Combo Cadillac Reformer twice weekly for 60 minutes over 8 consecutive weeks. The AI-assisted group received a programme revised each week by ChatGPT based on individual flexibility, balance, and muscular endurance data; the traditional group followed a fixed instructor-designed protocol throughout. Postural alignment was assessed using the Advanced Posture Evaluation and Correction System (APECS) at five anatomical landmarks (ears, shoulders, ASIS, knees, feet), and functional movement quality was assessed using all seven subtests of the Functional Movement Screen (FMS). The primary hypothesis was that AI-assisted weekly personalisation would produce superior improvements compared with the traditional protocol. Data were analysed using 2×2 mixed ANOVA with Holm-Bonferroni correction. Both groups showed statistically significant and large-magnitude improvements in all posture parameters and all FMS subtests over the 8-week period. However, neither the group main effect nor the Time × Group interaction reached significance for any outcome, indicating that the two programmes produced equivalent improvement trajectories. These findings suggest that the core principles of Reformer Pilates are the primary driver of adaptation, and that ChatGPT-based weekly programme personalisation did not confer a statistically significant advantage over traditional instruction within this sample size and intervention duration. This study is derived from the master's thesis of Bilge Gaye Yılmaz (Manisa Celal Bayar University, 2025; supervisor: Assoc. Prof. Dr. Naci Kalkan).

title: Sleep health impact and its projected productivity loss of secondhand smoke exposure among non-current smokers in China: an analysis of a 0.5-million prospective cohort
abstractText: Background: Prospective evidence on secondhand smoke (SHS) exposure and sleep health in adults is lacking, and the potential economic impact has not been quantified. We examined associations between SHS and sleep outcomes in a large Chinese cohort. Methods: From 512,724 adults aged 30–79 in the China Kadoorie Biobank (2004–2008), we analysed 346,222 non-smoking participants after excluding current smokers. Frequent SHS (≥1 day/week) was the primary exposure. Four sleep outcomes were assessed. Entropy-balanced logistic regression estimated odds ratios (ORs). Prospective analyses used data from resurvey (2013–2014; N=16,790). Changes of exposure status, different exposure settings, dose-response, and related productivity loss analyses were also conducted. Findings: Frequent SHS was associated with insufficient sleep (OR 1·26, 95% CI 1·22–1·29), early morning awakening (1·10, 1·07–1·13), and functional impairment (1·23, 1·17–1·29). Prospectively, baseline SHS predicted early morning awakening (1·24, 1·14–1·34) and functional impairment (1·23, 1·11–1·36). Persistently exposed participants had the highest odds (early morning awakening 1·53, 1·35–1·74), with a gradient consistent with a causal relationship. Household SHS showed the strongest association with difficulty falling asleep (1·47, 1·32–1·64). Under a scenario analysis assuming causality, approximately 12% of functional impairment was attributable to SHS, with projected annual productivity losses of 15·1 billion yuan (range 1·2–34·6 billion). Interpretation: Frequent SHS exposure is associated with poorer sleep health in non-smoking adults, with prospective and exposure-change evidence consistent with a causal relationship. A scenario analysis projected annual productivity losses of 15·1 billion yuan. China lacks a comprehensive national smoke-free law, and enforcement in public and workplace settings remains uneven. Strengthening smoke-free protections across public venues, workplaces, and homes could yield co-benefits for sleep health and productivity.

title: Blockage mechanisms of suspended particles in fractured ultra-low permeability reservoirs and optimization of water quality standards for post-fracturing injection
abstractText: Abstract The ecological and environmental management department requires the treatment of oilfield produced water to comply with the "Technical Requirements and Analysis Methods for Water Quality Indicators of Clastic Rock Reservoir Water Injection" SY/T 5329 − 2022. The water quality indicators of oilfield injected water (mainly suspended solids content, median suspended solids particle size, petroleum content, etc.) are strictly required, and the above water quality indicators are mainly determined based on the actual permeability of the reservoir. Hydraulic fracturing creates complex "pore-fracture" dual-media systems in ultra-low permeability reservoirs, but the blockage mechanisms of suspended solids during post-fracturing water injection remain unclear—rendering conventional homogeneous-media water quality standards inadequate. Using core samples and Brazilian splitting to simulate fractures, this study reveals distinct blockage behaviors of particles and oil droplets in fractured media. A critical particle-to-pore-throat diameter ratio (PC = 1.059) is identified to quantitatively distinguish internal pore blockage from external filter cake formation, bridging classical bridging theory with practical diagnosis. Fractures exhibit a dual effect: they mitigate overall permeability damage as preferential flow pathways, yet enable deep invasion of solids and oil, complicating subsequent removal. Orthogonal experiments with proppants demonstrate that stringent Class I standards can be relaxed to Class IV (particle size≤5µm, concentration≤25mg/L, oil content≤30mg/L) while maintaining permeability loss below 25%. By clarifying fracture-induced blockage mechanisms and validating relaxed standards, this study provides theoretical insights and practical guidance for cost-effective water injection in fractured ultra-low permeability reservoirs.

title: Translation uniformity and evolutionary conservation are associated with microprotein mass spectrometry detectability
abstractText: Abstract Background Non-canonical open reading frames (ncORFs) encode a substantial, largely unexplored layer of the human proteome. The short microproteins they produce frequently escape detection by standard mass spectrometry (MS) workflows, creating a “dark proteome” that hampers gene annotation and functional characterisation. To address this, sequence-derived attributes were used to identify factors associated with MS repository detectability and to build an interpretable predictive framework that enables rational prioritisation of ncORFs for proteomic discovery. Results 7,097 ncORF sequences (99% <150 residues) were curated from the TransCODE Consortium, and labelled by PeptideAtlas peptide-level evidence as MS-detected ( n = 1,725) or undetected ( n = 5,372). An ensemble combining ESM-2 protein language model embeddings with logistic regression and nineteen biological features (ESM2-LR) achieved a mean ROC-AUC of 0.721 (SD 0.018, coefficient of variation 2.5% across ten independent runs). Model-agnostic SHAP and permutation importance analyses concordantly ranked cumulative in-frame ribosome footprint uniformity (CIF-HBP) as the strongest associated factor, followed by mammalian ORF-level evolutionary conservation (ORBLv_mammal) and genomic biotype. Predicted HLA class I-binding peptide density, which captures physicochemical properties overlapping with optimal LC-MS/MS analyte characteristics, was also positively associated with detectability. Late-fusion analysis demonstrated that ESM-2 embeddings and biological features contribute complementary predictive signals. Conclusions These findings indicate that sustained translation, purifying selection for ORF structural integrity, and favourable peptide physicochemistry converge to influence ncORF detectability. The ESM2-LR framework provides a reproducible, scalable tool to prioritise candidate microproteins for targeted MS validation, gene annotation, and the interpretation of disease-associated regulatory variants, subject to future external validation on independent datasets.

title: Relationships between GPS-derived outdoor activity space ambient heat exposure, mental health, and salivary cortisol in a longitudinal, repeated measures sample of adult detroiters
abstractText: Exposure to heat in urban settings is a significant and growing public health concern. Yet, few studies have longitudinally measured everyday heat exposure using GPS-derived activity space data, paired with fine resolution satellite-derived heat measures, and no studies have measured effects on salivary cortisol in a community-dwelling sample. We address these gaps using data collected 2019-2023 across 11 neighborhoods in Detroit. Participants wore a GPS device and accelerometer over a one-week period. They completed a survey on demographics and mental health (anxiety and depression symptoms) and provided salivary cortisol samples (used to calculate diurnal slope) each year. We used a novel land surface temperature fusion product from ConstellR at daily cadence and 30-m spatial resolution to calculate heat exposure. We linked the seasonal time series of 2-band Enhanced Vegetation Index values calculated from the Harmonized Landsat-Sentinel-2 product with accumulated growing degree-days calculated from the ConstellR fusion product to model the land surface phenology at each pixel and used these modeled EVI2 values to estimate the exposure to greenness. We then tested whether higher heat exposure during routine daily outdoor activities was associated with poorer mental health or salivary cortisol data and whether these effects were attenuated by exposure to greenness. Among participants with ≥ 60 minutes of outdoor non-vehicle time, we observed a positive association between heat and anxiety (coef = 0.007, p-value = 0.062) and depression (coef = 0.007, p = 0.036) symptoms, after full confounder adjustment. Greenness was not independently, significantly associated with mental health measures and did not alter the effect size of heat exposure. We also observed a significant, positive association between heat exposure and cortisol slope (coef < 0.001, p-value = 0.029), indicative of higher stress. The consistency in our findings strengthens the evidence of the mental health impacts of everyday heat exposure, beyond extreme heat events. These findings have urban planning implications for increasing tree canopy, lowering impervious surfaces, providing heat shelters, and other urban cooling strategies. City-level or neighborhood-level heat action plans may help reduce the broader health impacts of rising temperatures in a warming climate.

title: Dependent autonomy: developing and refining a theoretical construct of managerial autonomy in healthcare
abstractText: Abstract Background Value-based healthcare (VBHC) frameworks, including the High-Value Health System (HVHS) model, emphasise structural components such as digital infrastructures, outcome measurement, and integrated care pathways. However, empirical evidence suggests that these components do not consistently translate into improved performance. This study addresses this gap by examining how system components are enacted in practice. Methods A theory-building design was employed, combining conceptual synthesis with empirical grounding in previously published studies of decentralised healthcare governance and hybrid management. An abductive analytical approach was used to integrate insights from decision space theory, organisational theory, and VBHC frameworks. Results The analysis resulted in a conceptual framework identifying dependent autonomy as the central mechanism linking system design to practice. HVHS components were found to operate indirectly through organisational systems, which function as dual mechanisms that both enable and constrain managerial action. Dependent autonomy, defined as the extent to which managerial autonomy is contingent upon organisational systems, determines the effective enactment of coordination and patient flows. Variation in VBHC outcomes is thus explained by differences in how organisational systems shape decision space. Conclusions This study reframes healthcare transformation as a problem of organisational enactment rather than system design. By introducing dependent autonomy, it extends decision space theory and integrates it with organisational and VBHC perspectives. The findings highlight that the effectiveness of healthcare reforms depends on the organisational conditions that make system components actionable, offering a theoretically grounded explanation for variability in implementation outcomes.

title: Venous infarction mimicking brain tumour: recognition of the sulcal tram-track appearance and gyriform diffusion restriction, a retrospective study
abstractText: Abstract Purpose Venous infarctions can demonstrate varied imaging appearances and in certain cases, they may mimic intracranial tumors/space occupying lesions, leading to diagnostic confusion and potentially unnecessary invasive procedures. The purpose of this study was to describe the neuroimaging features of venous infarction presenting as tumor-like cortical lesions and to highlight a distinctive imaging appearance termed the Sulcal Tram-Track Sign. Methods A retrospective review was performed of patients with venous infarcts presenting as focal cortical lesions suggestive of space-occupying pathology on MRI. Imaging features were analyzed on conventional MRI sequences, diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI), and susceptibility-weighted imaging (SWI). Particular attention was given to lesion morphology, relationship to cortical sulci, diffusion characteristics, susceptibility findings, and enhancement patterns. Results Eleven patients were identified with venous infarction where the lesions were predominantly cortically based and mimicked space occupying lesions. T2-weighted imaging demonstrated paired linear hyperintensities along opposing banks of the affected sulcus in all cases, producing a tram-track appearance. Gyriform diffusion restriction was present in most patients, and susceptibility-weighted imaging demonstrated cord sign corresponding to thrombosed cortical veins in the majority of cases. Contrast enhancement was minimal or absent. Conclusion Venous infarction due to cortical vein thrombosis may mimic intracranial tumors on MRI. Recognition of the Sulcal Tram-Track Sign, along with associated diffusion restriction and susceptibility changes, may facilitate early diagnosis and help avoid unnecessary invasive interventions.

title: Investigation on laser-assisted ultra-precision cutting process technology for SiCp/Al composites
abstractText: Abstract Medium-volume-fraction SiCp/Al composites are premier candidates for optical components, yet their application is constrained by severe surface defects like particle pull-out and interfacial debonding. To address these challenges, an optimized laser-assisted machining (LAM) strategy is employed. Distinct from purely mechanical assistants that primarily focus on force reduction, LAM leverages selective thermal softening to create a compliant buffer within the aluminum matrix, thereby reducing the surface roughness Sa to 0.023 µm. Utilizing constitutive models calibrated via quasi-static and high-temperature dynamic tests, finite element analysis reveals that LAM-induced thermal softening of the matrix reduces interfacial stress concentration and suppresses SiCp/Al interfacial debonding, minimizing particle pull-out and subsequent secondary plowing effects. Furthermore, a novel surface quality evaluation scheme utilizing reconstructed three-dimensional point clouds is developed to quantify cavity defects, effectively addressing the limitations of conventional roughness metrics.

title: Epidemiology and associated factors of Lophomonas blattarum infection in patients undergoing bronchoscopy: a cross-sectional study
abstractText: Abstract Background and aim: Pulmonary infection caused by Lophomonas blattarum has been increasingly recognized as an emerging parasitic disease in several Asian countries, including Iran. This flagellated protozoan is a commensal organism of the intestinal tract of insects and, under certain conditions, may act as an opportunistic pathogen leading to respiratory infections, particularly among patients with chronic pulmonary disorders. This study aimed to evaluate the prevalence and to characterize the clinical, epidemiological, and therapeutic features of Lophomonas infection in patients with chronic respiratory diseases undergoing bronchoscopy. Methods present cross-sectional descriptive-analytical study included 88 patients with chronic respiratory diseases who underwent bronchoscopy. Data were obtained through systematic medical record review and structured telephone follow-up. Statistical analyses were performed using SPSS software. Results Of the 88 patients, 23 (26.1%) were diagnosed with Lophomonas blattarum infection. No statistically significant association was observed between infection status and demographic variables such as age or sex (P > 0.05). However, exposure to potential vectors, including cockroaches, birds, and rodents, was significantly associated with infection (P = 0.001). The most frequently reported respiratory symptoms were cough (79.5%), dyspnea (72.7%), and sputum production (51%). Among infected patients, 82.6% showed a favorable response to metronidazole therapy, while age and sex did not significantly influence treatment outcomes. Conclusion Lophomonas infection demonstrates a notable prevalence among patients with chronic respiratory diseases, particularly in populations with increased environmental exposure to potential vectors. Early recognition and appropriate treatment, especially with metronidazole, may result in significant clinical improvement. These findings underscore the necessity for improved diagnostic accuracy, enhanced screening strategies, and effective environmental control measures for the prevention and management of this emerging infection.

title: Selective nerve block-guided bilateral T10 nerve root transection using unilateral biportal endoscopy for persistent severe intercostal neuralgia caused by cement leakage after percutaneous vertebroplasty: a case report and literature review
abstractText: Abstract Background : Symptomatic cement leakage after percutaneous vertebroplasty (PVP) is uncommon but may cause severe radicular pain or neurological deficits when the leaked cement involves the spinal canal or neural foramen. Thoracic foraminal cement leakage presenting as refractory intercostal neuralgia is particularly rare, and identifying the responsible nerve root can be challenging when multiple adjacent foramina are involved. Case presentation: An 83-year-old woman underwent PVP for fresh osteoporotic compression fractures of T10 and L5. Her preoperative low back pain resolved completely after PVP; however, she immediately developed severe bilateral intercostal neuralgia radiating from the costal arches to the periumbilical region, with a visual analog scale score of 8. Computed tomography showed cement leakage into the bilateral T9/10 and T10/11 foraminal regions. Because imaging alone could not reliably determine the symptomatic level, staged bilateral selective nerve block was performed. Bilateral T9/10 foraminal block did not relieve the pain, whereas bilateral T10/11 foraminal block produced marked pain relief, indicating that the bilateral T10 nerve roots were responsible. After failed conservative treatment, unilateral biportal endoscopic bilateral T10 nerve root transection was performed. Intraoperatively, only a limited amount of cement that obstructed nerve root exposure was removed, followed by targeted transection of the bilateral T10 nerve roots under endoscopic visualization. The patient’s intercostal neuralgia resolved immediately after surgery, and no recurrence or major surgery-related complication was observed at the 3-month follow-up. Conclusion : In patients with symptomatic cement leakage after PVP, imaging findings may not always correspond to the responsible pain-generating level, especially when multiple adjacent foramina are involved. Selective nerve block may provide useful functional evidence for identifying the symptomatic nerve root. For carefully selected patients with refractory thoracic radicular pain, unilateral biportal endoscopic nerve root transection may represent an individualized salvage option when complete cement removal is unnecessary or associated with excessive surgical risk. However, because nerve root transection is irreversible, strict patient selection, reliable localization, adequate risk assessment, and informed consent are essential.

title: Single-cell and spatial transcriptomics define a C3-centred multicellular ecology in colorectal liver metastasis
abstractText: Abstract Colorectal liver metastasis (CRLM) is shaped by malignant-cell plasticity and microenvironmental remodeling, but how malignant, stromal, vascular and myeloid states assemble spatially remains unclear. We sought to define recurrent multicellular programs associated with CRLM. We integrated a 136,995-cell single-cell atlas with copy-number inference, consensus non-negative matrix factorization, regulatory-network and patient-aligned trajectory analyses, intercellular-communication modeling, four Visium sections, bulk-cohort survival analyses, virtual knockout, connectivity-map screening and molecular docking. Three malignant epithelial programs were resolved along a C1-to-C2-to-C3 continuum. The rare C3 state displayed secretory, invasive and epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition features and was associated with shorter recurrence-free survival. Fib- COL10A1 fibroblasts and Endo- GJA5 endothelial cells formed a recurrent stromal–vascular scaffold, whereas CTSL -program macrophages occupied focal interfaces whose geometry varied among metastases. Spatial pathway and multiview analyses implicated MAPK- and VEGF-associated activity. An INHBA – CST6 – LBH – FSTL3 score was associated with recurrence in TCGA and showed partial external validation. Virtual knockout indicated convergent CST6 / LBH network effects, and connectivity-map analysis nominated PD-0325901 as a candidate for reversing the associated state; docking provided exploratory structural support for CST6 but not LBH . These analyses define a spatially flexible C3-centred ecology and a MAPK-linked network vulnerability in CRLM. The framework is computational and requires experimental validation.

title: Kinetic Acceleration and the Stoichiometric Limit Dictate the Behavior of Reactivity-Enhanced Step-Growth Polymerization
abstractText: Abstract For nearly a century, the Carothers equation and Flory’s equal-reactivity assumption have governed our fundamental understanding of step-growth polymerization, dictating that (ultra)high-molecular-weight polymers strictly demand stoichiometric equivalence. However, the recent emergence of reactivity-enhanced step-growth polymerization, known as nonstoichiometric polycondensation, contradicts this classical paradigm by producing (ultra)high-molecular-weight polymers under stoichiometric imbalances. Herein, we resolve this empirical paradox by deriving an elegant, closed-form algebraic expression, Xn(α, r, p), based on the steady-state approximation. This compact formula explicitly quantifies how the degree of polymerization (Xn) is co-determined by kinetic acceleration factor (α), stoichiometric ratio (r), and monomer conversion (p). Through rigorous mathematical derivation, we explicitly decouple the polymerization behavior into kinetic acceleration and stoichiometric limits. The resulting formulation elucidates their intricate interplay, revealing how the former systematically delays molecular end-capping to circumvent classical stoichiometric limitations. Counterintuitively, we demonstrate that the optimal critical stoichiometry is not a fixed constant, but a dynamic trajectory continuously evolving with time or monomer conversion—overturning the long-held assumption of a static optimum. The predictions of our framework are validated against previously experimental observations, successfully resolving the stoichiometric paradox. Ultimately, this theoretical framework not only reshapes our understanding of step-growth polymerization by moving beyond the classically stoichiometry-dominated paradigm, instead revealing a profound synergistic interplay between kinetics and stoichiometry but also provides a solid foundation to rationally design and synthesize advanced polymeric materials.

title: Divergent bandgap responses in Cu- and Zn-doped NiTiO3 nanoparticles
abstractText: Abstract Nickel titanate (NiTiO 3 ) nanoparticles doped with Cu and Zn were successfully synthesized via a modified Pechini sol-gel method to investigate the influence of dopant electronic configuration on the structural, optical, and photocatalytic properties of NiTiO 3 . The synthesized materials were systematically characterized using X-ray diffraction (XRD), Raman spectroscopy, scanning electron microscopy (SEM), high-resolution transmission electron microscopy (HR-TEM), and UV–Vis diffuse reflectance spectroscopy. Structural analyses confirmed the formation of phase-pure rhombohedral NiTiO 3 with nanocrystalline morphology, while the result revealed slight lattice expansion resulting from the substitution of larger Cu 2+ and Zn 2+ ions at the Ni site without altering the host crystal structure. Optical investigations demonstrated distinctly different electronic responses for the two dopants. Cu doping produced a pronounced redshift in the absorption edge and reduced the optical band gap from approximately 2.1 to 1.75 eV, whereas Zn doping caused negligible changes in the band gap. This contrasting behavior is attributed to the partially filled Cu 2+ (3d 9 ) electronic configuration, which introduces Cu 3d-derived impurity states and enhances O 2p-Cu 3d hybridization near the valence band, while the fully filled Zn 2+ (3d 10 ) configuration does not significantly modify the electronic structure. The improved electronic structure of Cu-doped NiTiO 3 resulted in superior visible-light photocatalytic performance toward cationic thiazine dye degradation. These findings demonstrate that dopant electronic configuration plays a decisive role in tailoring the band structure and photocatalytic activity of NiTiO 3 , providing an effective strategy for designing high-performance visible-light-responsive oxide photocatalysts.

title: Alkaloid-rich extracts from Ocimum gratissimum and Zanthoxylum zanthoxyloides as potential antibiotic adjuvants against resistant bacterial pathogens
abstractText: Abstract Background Ocimum gratissimum and Zanthoxylum zanthoxyloides are medicinal plants widely used in African traditional medicine for the treatment of infectious diseases. The increasing prevalence of antimicrobial resistance (AMR) has renewed interest in plant-derived bioactive compounds as potential antibacterial agents and antibiotic adjuvants capable of restoring or enhancing the efficacy of existing antibiotics. Aim of the study This study investigated the antibacterial activity of total alkaloid extracts from O. gratissimum (OG-TAE) and Z. zanthoxyloides (ZZ-TAE), and evaluated their ability to modulate the efficacy of tetracycline against selected bacterial pathogens. Materials and methods Total alkaloid extracts from O. gratissimum (OG-TAE, 1.18% w/w) and Z. zanthoxyloides (ZZ-TAE, 1.40% w/w) were evaluated against Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria using checkerboard and time–kill kinetic assays. The chemical composition of the extracts was characterized by LC–ESI–MS analysis to identify putative bioactive alkaloids associated with antibacterial activity. Results Both extracts exhibited strain-dependent bacteriostatic activity with greater potency against Gram-positive bacteria. OG-TAE enhanced tetracycline activity against Salmonella poona , producing additive interactions and reducing the antibiotic concentrations required for antibacterial activity. Time–kill studies confirmed bactericidal effects for the combinations, with 5–10-fold improvements in antibacterial activity comparable to ciprofloxacin after 24 h. LC–ESI–MS analysis identified the following bioactive alkaloids; Zanthoamide I, nor-chelerythrine, 8-acetonyldihydro-chelerythrine, skimmianine, and benzimidazol-5-amine. Conclusions These findings demonstrate the potential of alkaloid-rich extracts from O. gratissimum and Z. zanthoxyloides as effective antibiotic adjuvants that enhance tetracycline efficacy, enable antibiotic dose reduction and offer a plant-based combination strategy to combat AMR.

title: PENDAMPINGAN TRANSFORMASI DIGITAL MELALUI PENGEMBANGAN DAN IMPLEMENTASI WEBSITE EDOTEL DI SMK NEGERI 2 GORONTALO
abstractText: SMK Negeri 2 Gorontalo memiliki edOTEL sebagai unit hotel latih yang berfungsi sebagai sarana pembelajaran praktik bagi siswa Kompetensi Keahlian Perhotelan. Namun, pengelolaan edOTEL masih menghadapi kendala berupa promosi konvensional, pencatatan reservasi kamar secara manual, dan latihan praktik front office berbasis dokumen kertas. Kondisi tersebut menyebabkan proses administrasi kurang efisien dan belum optimal dalam mendukung kesiapan siswa menghadapi sistem perhotelan digital. Kegiatan pengabdian kepada masyarakat ini bertujuan mengembangkan, menyosialisasikan, dan mengimplementasikan website edOTEL yang mengintegrasikan fungsi promosi, manajemen reservasi berbasis web, dan e-learning simulasi praktik front office. Kegiatan dilaksanakan selama Mei–Juli 2026 dengan melibatkan 58 peserta, terdiri atas 8 guru/pengelola dan 50 siswa Kompetensi Keahlian Perhotelan. Metode pelaksanaan menggunakan pendekatan Participatory Action Learning yang dipadukan dengan Software Development Life Cycle (SDLC) model Waterfall, meliputi analisis kebutuhan, perancangan, pengembangan dan pengujian, pelatihan, serta evaluasi. Hasil kegiatan menunjukkan bahwa landing page, sistem manajemen reservasi, modul e-learning front office, serta sosialisasi dan distribusi panduan digital mencapai ketercapaian 100%, sedangkan integrasi payment gateway mencapai 60%. Evaluasi terhadap 58 responden menunjukkan tingkat penerimaan dan kelayakan sistem sebesar 87,91% dengan kategori sangat layak. Dengan demikian, website edOTEL mampu meningkatkan efisiensi administrasi dan promosi serta mendukung pembelajaran digital terapan dalam ekosistem Teaching Factory

title: Multidimensional Competitive Psychological Profile of Indonesian Women’s National Football Team Athletes Following Competition
abstractText: Background & objective: Competitive psychological functioning in elite football is multidimensional, involving cognitive and somatic anxiety, self-confidence, and concentration. Evidence integrating these dimensions among elite female national-team football athletes remains limited, particularly in Southeast Asia. This study aimed to characterize the post-competition psychological profile of Indonesian Women’s National Football Team athletes and explore differences according to playing position. Materials & Methods: A quantitative descriptive observational study involved 22 athletes selected through total sampling. Psychological responses were assessed immediately after competition using the 20-item Athlete Anxiety Questionnaire (AAQ), measuring cognitive anxiety, somatic anxiety, self-confidence, and concentration. Descriptive statistics characterized the psychological profile. Positional differences among goalkeepers, defenders, midfielders, and forwards were explored using the Kruskal–Wallis H test, with epsilon-squared (ε²) as the omnibus effect size. Holm-adjusted pairwise comparisons were conducted where appropriate. Results: Cognitive anxiety averaged 16.55 ± 2.79, with 81.8% of athletes classified as moderate, while somatic anxiety averaged 7.68 ± 1.13, also with 81.8% classified as moderate. Self-confidence was relatively high (22.23 ± 2.22), with 81.8% classified as high, whereas concentration averaged 14.14 ± 2.12, with 63.6% classified as moderate. The descriptive anxiety composite averaged 24.23 ± 3.57. No significant positional differences were found for cognitive anxiety, somatic anxiety, or the anxiety composite. Significant omnibus differences were observed for self-confidence, H(3) = 8.208, p = .042, ε² = .289, and concentration, H(3) = 10.752, p = .013, ε² = .431; however, no pairwise differences remained significant after Holm adjustment. Conclusions: The athletes demonstrated moderate cognitive and somatic anxiety, high self-confidence, and predominantly moderate concentration following competition. These findings support multidimensional psychological assessment in elite football. Positional findings should be considered exploratory given the small, unequal subgroups and absence of significant adjusted pairwise differences.

title: Learning to remember: advances in memory mechanisms for large language models
abstractText: Abstract Memory has become a central mechanism for extending large language models (LLMs) beyond fixed context windows, stateless interaction, and static parametric knowledge. This survey organizes the literature around three complementary dimensions: the life cycle of memory, the storage substrate, and the system role that memory plays in LLM-based agents, while using cognitive-science-inspired memory concepts as a lightweight conceptual motivation rather than as a separate technical contribution or implementation family. On this basis, we distinguish three mechanism families: nonparametric memory, where information is stored outside model parameters in text, graph, multimodal, or database-like structures; parametric memory, where information is stored or accessed through activations, key-value caches, learned modules, adapter-based parameterizations, or model weights; and memory for agent evolution, where stored experiences support reinforcement learning, continual learning, procedural reuse, context engineering, and agent harness design. Evaluation is treated as a separate cross-cutting component rather than as a memory mechanism. Unlike surveys that focus primarily on retrieval-augmented generation or long-context modeling, this paper emphasizes the full memory life cycle: construction, maintenance, retrieval, consolidation, forgetting, governance, and evaluation. By aligning conceptual motivations, computational memory mechanisms, benchmarks, and deployment concerns, the survey provides a structured roadmap for designing memory-augmented LLM agents that are persistent, adaptive, auditable, and safe to update over time.

title: Depression, anxiety, stress, and intolerance of uncertainty during the COVID-19 pandemic by considering the impact of pre-existing mental health issues
abstractText: Purpose This research was conducted during the COVID-19 pandemic. This study aims to investigate self-reported mental health issues in a public sample, including depression, anxiety and intolerance of uncertainty about the future. Design/methodology/approach A public sample (N = 313) was obtained through social media, and collected using an online survey. Participants completed a series of demographic questions including disclosure about previous mental health issues, the depression anxiety stress scale (DASS) and the intolerance uncertainty scale (IUS). Findings There was a strong positive relationship between elements of the DASS and IUS. Having previous mental health issues were strongly associated with higher scores across all measures. Originality/value Evidence is provided to support the notion that additional stress, anxiety and fear is experienced by people with pre-existing mental health issues during unprecedented times. This research offers a unique insight into the mental health of the general public during a global pandemic.

title: Associations between skeletal muscle-to-visceral fat ratio and depression symptom severity among cancer survivors: an examination of mediation pathways using the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) 2011–2018
abstractText: Abstract Background Depression is highly prevalent among individuals diagnosed with cancer and associated with reduced wellbeing, physical function, and increased mortality risk. Emerging evidence suggests that physiological factors such as body composition and systemic inflammation are associated with symptom severity and may help identify individuals diagnosed with cancer who are at greater risk of depression. This study examined whether the skeletal muscle-to-visceral fat ratio (SVR) is associated with depressive symptom severity in cancer survivors, and whether inflammatory biomarkers and behavioral factors mediate this relationship. Methods This cross-sectional analysis of 541 adult cancer survivors, obtained from National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES, 2011–2018), examined associations between body composition, inflammation, and depression symptom severity. Body composition was indexed by SVR (DEXA-derived), inflammation was assessed via white blood cell (WBC) count and high sensitivity C-reactive proteins (HS-CRP), and depression symptom severity was measured using the Patient Health Questionnaire-9 (PHQ-9). Complex sample generalized linear models examined associations between predictors and PHQ-9, followed by mediation analyses testing WBC, HS-CRP, and physical activity as mediators. Results SVR was significantly and inversely associated with PHQ-9 scores in unadjusted ( b = − 0.501, 95% CI − 0.937, − 0.064, p = 0.025) and partially adjusted models ( b = − 0.590, 95% CI − 1.102, − 0.077, p = 0.025), attenuating after full adjustment ( b = − 0.423, 95% CI − 0.980, 0.134, p = 0.134). WBC showed no association with PHQ-9 at any stage, while HS-CRP showed a similar pattern to SVR. SVR was significantly associated with WBC and HS-CRP, mediation analyses found no significant indirect effects through WBC/physical activity. Pathway estimates were not fully identified due to a hypothesized causal link between physical activity and WBC. Conclusion Favorable body composition was associated with lower depressive symptom severity and biomarkers of inflammation in this population of cancer survivors. These relationships attenuate after adjustment. Neither HS-CRP nor physical activity/WBC showed clear evidence of mediating this association, suggesting that other or more complex mechanisms underpin the link between body composition and depression severity in cancer survivors.

title: Study protocol: outcomes of REvision surgery after primary JOINt replacement (REJOIN) study
abstractText: Aims The number of arthroplasty revision surgeries is increasing, yet patient-centred outcomes such as mental wellbeing, fulfilment of expectations for postoperative outcomes such as pain, function, and activities of daily living, as outlined in the Hospital for Special Surgery Knee Scale (HSS), and the Hip/Knee Replacement Expectations Survey (HRES/KRES), as well as the importance patients assign to such outcomes, remain insufficiently understood. Moreover, little is known about the role of their significant others. While essential to patients’ recovery and wellbeing, they may experience substantial emotional and practical burdens themselves. Here we present the protocol of the REJOIN study (Outcomes of REvision surgery after primary JOINt replacement), which aims to examine the impact of revision surgery on patients and their significant others. The study describes patients’ expectations and their fulfilment, mental wellbeing, functional outcomes, and the perceived value of outcomes following surgery, as well as the health-related quality of life (QoL) and caregiver burden experienced by their significant others. In addition, it investigates risk factors associated with the aforementioned outcomes. Methods This will be a multicentre, longitudinal observational study. All eligible patients scheduled for revision surgery after total hip or knee arthroplasty between March 2026 and February 2033 are invited to participate together with their significant other. We aim to include 3,650 patients. Data will be gathered preoperatively, and at three, six, 12, and 24 months. Results The main outcome parameters are expectations and their fulfilment, measured through three different data sources: patient-reported outcome measures (PROMs) gathered for usual care, patients’ medical files, and study questionnaires. The PROMs comprise of the HSS, HRES/KRES, mental health (Pain Catastrophizing Scale (PCS), Hospital Anxiety and Depression Screen (HADS)), QoL (EuroQol five-dimension questionnaire (EQ-5D)), pain (Numeric Rating Scale (NRS) pain), hip/knee functioning (Oxford Hip Score/Oxford Knee Score (OHS/OKS)), patient-prioritized importance of outcomes (their top three), strain on significant other (CarerQol-7D), positive experiences of significant other (PES), and hip/knee function according to significant other (OHS/OKS by significant other). Conclusion The REJOIN study offers a systematic approach to evaluate the impact of revision surgery on patients and their significant others with regard to expectation fulfilment, mental wellbeing, and functional outcome. title: Rhetorical structure and authorial positioning in medical research article introductions: a corpus-based comparison of articles published in selected Vietnamese and international journals
abstractText: This study compares rhetorical structure and selected resources of authorial positioning in 154 English-language medical research article introductions published during 2021–2025. The Vietnamese and international journal samples contain 89 and 65 articles, with 37,650 and 34,452 Introduction words. An adapted CARS inventory identifies rhetorical functions; hedges and self-mentions are examined alongside a separate grammatical measure of overt be-passives. Explicit knowledge gaps occur in 66.3% and 93.8% of introductions, respectively (Holm-adjusted p<.001). Continuation of earlier work is also more frequent in the final IJI coding, although this category requires context-sensitive interpretation. None of the three linguistic comparisons reaches the adjusted .05 threshold. The findings provide examples for teaching research justification and author positioning. Sample composition and context-sensitive coding limit broader inference.

title: Challenges Faced by Parents in Raising Children with Special Needs: A Narrative Literature Review
abstractText: Parents raising children with special needs face interconnected psychological, physical, social, financial, and service-related challenges. This narrative literature review aimed to synthesize evidence on parental difficulties, influencing factors, coping strategies, and support needs. Fifteen empirical studies published between 2019 and 2026 were selected through eligibility screening and qualitative appraisal. Data were extracted using a structured matrix and analyzed through thematic narrative synthesis. The findings showed that parents commonly experienced emotional distress, fatigue, stigma, social isolation, financial pressure, employment disruption, family strain, and limited access to healthcare, rehabilitation, and inclusive education. The severity of these challenges was shaped by the child’s condition, parental knowledge, coping capacity, family support, socioeconomic status, cultural beliefs, geographical location, and service accessibility. Parents used acceptance, information seeking, spiritual practices, advocacy, structured routines, and social support. The review highlights the need for continuous family-centered services integrating psychological, educational, financial, professional, workplace, and policy support. Ultimately, establishing robust policy frameworks and fostering cross-sectoral collaboration among healthcare providers, educators, and community leaders are essential to mitigate systemic barriers, alleviate caregiver burnout, and promote holistic family resilience. Furthermore, future empirical research must prioritize longitudinal methodologies to evaluate the sustainable real-world efficacy, accessibility, and scalability of culturally tailored intervention programs across diverse socioeconomic landscapes.

title: Social - emotional competence among lower secondary students: evidence from Da Nang, Vietnam
abstractText: Social-emotional competence plays a crucial role in the holistic development of students, especially at the lower secondary school age – a period of significant psychophysiological changes. This study surveys the current state of social-emotional competence among 332 students at Le Do Secondary School, Da Nang. The study uses the Social-Emotional Competency Questionnaire which comprises five component competencies: self-awareness, self-management, social awareness, social interaction, and responsible decision-making. Analysis using SPSS 30.0 software shows that students' social-emotional competence ranges from average to high. Social interaction and social awareness are the highest-ranking competencies, while self-management remains limited. The study also reveals significant differences in social-emotional competence based on gender, grade level, and academic achievement. These results provide educational stakeholders with a basis for developing appropriate educational strategies.

title: Effects of Vacuum and Modified Atmosphere Packaging on Physicochemical and Microbiological Quality of Cooked Squid Stuffed with Sticky Rice During Refrigerated Storage
abstractText: Stuffed squid with sticky rice (Tupa Sutong) is a traditional seafood product from southern Thailand with limited refrigerated shelf life because of rapid microbial spoilage and quality deterioration. This study evaluated the effects of atmospheric packaging (AP), vacuum packaging (VP), and modified atmosphere packaging (MAP; 50% O₂, 25% CO₂, and 25% N₂) on the physicochemical and microbiological quality of cooked stuffed squid during refrigerated storage (4 ± 2 °C) for 24 days. Changes in hardness, pH, total volatile basic nitrogen (TVB-N), trimethylamine nitrogen (TMA-N), thiobarbituric acid (TBA), and total viable count (TVC) were determined throughout storage. Storage time significantly affected all quality parameters (p 0.05). Samples stored under AP deteriorated most rapidly, showing faster increases in TVB-N, TMA-N, TBA, and TVC, accompanied by a greater reduction in texture quality. Both VP and MAP delayed quality deterioration by slowing microbial growth and chemical changes during storage. Based on the microbiological acceptability limit, the shelf life of the product was 12, 18, and 21 days under AP, MAP, and VP, respectively. Among the packaging systems evaluated, VP provided the greatest extension of refrigerated shelf life while maintaining the physicochemical and microbiological quality of cooked stuffed squid with sticky rice. These findings provide useful information for selecting appropriate packaging systems for the commercial production and distribution of this traditional seafood product.

title: Đánh giá ấn tượng thị giác đối với giao diện ứng dụng mẹ và bé bằng tiếp cận Kansei: hàm ý sơ bộ cho thiết kế ứng dụng chăm sóc thai sản
abstractText: Nghiên cứu đánh giá thăm dò ấn tượng thị giác đối với năm bộ giao diện ứng dụng mẹ và bé nhằm cung cấp cơ sở định hướng cho thiết kế giao diện ứng dụng chăm sóc thai sản. Khảo sát 126 người tham gia sử dụng 10 cặp từ Kansei đối cực trên thang 5 mức để đánh giá các bộ giao diện A–E. Dữ liệu được phân tích bằng điểm trung bình, độ lệch chuẩn, Cronbach’s alpha, kiểm định Friedman và Wilcoxon signed-rank với hiệu chỉnh Holm. Kết quả cho thấy D và E có điểm Kansei tổng hợp cao hơn A, B và C, trong khi khác biệt giữa D và E không có ý nghĩa thống kê. Cronbach’s alpha dao động từ 0,974 đến 0,978. Phân tích giới hạn ở 76 người thuộc hai nhóm người dùng trọng tâm vẫn duy trì xu hướng D/E cao hơn A/B/C. Đồng thời, so sánh trực tiếp giữa mẹ bầu và mẹ đang nuôi con nhỏ không ghi nhận khác biệt có ý nghĩa trong đánh giá từng giao diện. Kết quả được diễn giải ở cấp độ ấn tượng tổng thể và gợi ý các hàm ý thiết kế sơ bộ về độ thoáng và các cảm nhận liên quan đến tin cậy và an toàn.

title: A novel SDHA L511P variant: evidence supporting reclassification to likely pathogenic
Renal cell carcinoma organoids: establishment, applications, and clinical translation—current evidence, technical challenges, and future directions
abstractText: Renal cell carcinoma (RCC) is characterized by marked histological, molecular, and spatial heterogeneity, which contributes to substantial interpatient variability in responses to targeted therapies, immune checkpoint inhibitors, and combination regimens. Conventional two-dimensional cultures and animal models are limited in their ability to simultaneously recapitulate patient-specific tumor features, maintain biological fidelity, and support experimental throughput. Tumor organoids can be expanded in three-dimensional culture while retaining, to varying degrees, the histological and molecular characteristics of their tumors of origin, thereby providing a complementary platform for RCC disease modeling, investigation of drug resistance mechanisms, and functional drug testing. This review is structured according to the source of evidence and the maturity of clinical translation. We summarize the establishment, culture, and quality assessment of RCC patient-derived organoids, three-dimensional tumor spheroids, stem cell-derived kidney organoids, air–liquid interface cultures, and organ-on-chip models, with particular emphasis on distinguishing direct evidence from RCC organoid studies, mechanistic evidence from non-organoid RCC models, and methodological evidence derived from other cancer types. Current evidence supports the use of RCC organoids for preserving tumor phenotypes, investigating tumor heterogeneity, evaluating responses to targeted therapies, and validating mechanisms of drug resistance. However, clinical translation remains limited by variable model-establishment efficiency and stability, incomplete recapitulation of the tumor microenvironment, and insufficient validation against patient outcomes. Future research should improve model representativeness through multiregional and longitudinal sampling, chemically defined matrices, multicellular co-culture systems, vascularized and microfluidic platforms, automated high-content screening, and single-cell and spatial multi-omics approaches. Analytical validity, clinical validity, and clinical utility should be evaluated as distinct but complementary dimensions of translational performance. At present, RCC organoids are best positioned as tools for mechanistic investigation and adjunctive prioritization of therapeutic options rather than as standalone platforms for treatment decision-making independent of pathological classification, molecular testing, and established clinical guidelines.

title: The relationship of parental acceptance-rejection and perceived social support with depressive symptoms and self-confidence in LGBT+ individuals
abstractText: Purpose This study aims to examine the relationships between parental acceptance and rejection and perceived social support variables and depressive symptoms and self-confidence in LGBT+ young adults living in Turkey. Design/methodology/approach A cross-sectional correlational online survey was conducted with 126 LGBT+ young adults aged 18–35 living in Turkey. Participants completed scales measuring maternal and paternal acceptance and rejection, perceived social support, depressive symptoms and self-confidence. Pearson correlations and four two-step hierarchical regression analyses were applied to examine the relationships between the variables. Using reverse-order hierarchical regressions, the additional variance explained by the parental rejection variable was evaluated after controlling for perceived social support. Maternal and paternal rejection coefficients were directly compared using linear contrasts. Finally, age and employment status were controlled for in sensitivity analyses, and HC3 robust standard errors were applied. Findings A total of 51.6% of participants scored at or above the Beck Depression Inventory cutoff. Perceived social support was significantly associated with lower depressive symptoms and higher self-confidence (all p = 0.001). Maternal rejection maintained a significant association with depressive symptoms (ß = 0.275, p = 0.002) and self-confidence (ß = −0.182, p = 0.044) after controlling for social support. Paternal rejection was significant in the initial models but was no longer statistically significant when social support was added. In reverse-order hierarchical regression analyses, maternal rejection explained significant additional variance in both outcome variables after controlling for social support. Paternal rejection did not contribute significantly. In the direct comparison, maternal and paternal rejection coefficients differed significantly for self-confidence, but not for depressive symptoms. Sensitivity analyses generally supported the main findings. However, when we used robust HC3 standard errors, the association between maternal rejection and self-confidence lost statistical significance. Research limitations/implications The cross-sectional design prevents causal interpretation of the observed associations. The relatively young, predominantly university–student sample and convenience-based online recruitment may also limit generalisability. Because all core variables were assessed using self-report measures, common method variance and social desirability bias should be considered. In addition, multiple regression analyses increased the risk of Type I error. Future research should replicate these findings using larger and more diverse samples, longitudinal designs and confirmatory analyses to clarify the temporal relationships among parental rejection, social support, depressive symptoms and self-confidence. Practical implications The findings highlight the importance of considering parental rejection and perceived social support variables in the psychological assessment of LGBT+ young adults. However, because the design is cross-sectional, causal inferences cannot be made. Social implications The findings highlight the importance of supportive family and social environments for the psychological well-being of LGBT+ young adults. Greater perceived social support was consistently associated with fewer depressive symptoms and higher self-confidence, suggesting that strengthening access to supportive relationships may be particularly relevant for this population. The persistent associations of maternal rejection with both outcomes also underscore the potential value of family-focused psychoeducation, counselling and social support initiatives aimed at reducing rejecting responses and promoting more affirming family relationships. Originality/value This study extends previous LGBT+ mental health research by distinguishing maternal from paternal acceptance-rejection rather than combining parental experiences into a single construct. It also examines self-confidence as a distinct outcome, an area less frequently studied than self-esteem. In addition, the study tests the incremental contribution of perceived social support beyond parental acceptance-rejection across depressive symptoms and self-confidence. The results show that maternal rejection retained unique associations with both outcomes, whereas paternal rejection did not after social support was entered, highlighting potentially different parental patterns.
