title: Double-sided printed terahertz collimating metalens mounted on a resonant tunneling diode
abstractText: Abstract Integrating optically thin metasurfaces with continuous-wave (CW) terahertz sources offers an alternative to conventional bulky optical elements for manipulating terahertz waves. However, planar optical elements composed of metasurfaces have yet to be actively adopted in CW terahertz sources due to limited fabrication methods suitable for micrometer-scale meta-atoms. Here, we fabricate two types of printed terahertz collimating metalenses on cyclo-olefin polymer and polyimide films using super inkjet printing. The fabricated metalenses are composed of double-sided printed metal patches on dielectric films, enabling simultaneous control of the electric and magnetic fields while maintaining an optically thin structure. The printed terahertz collimating metalenses fabricated on cyclo-olefin polymer and polyimide films enhance the directivity of a resonant tunneling diode oscillating at 0.312 THz to 2.29 and 1.46 times, respectively. Our results demonstrate advanced wavefront control of CW terahertz sources using inkjet-printed planar optical elements. The fabrication method for terahertz planar optical elements proposed in this paper will be a welcome contribution to terahertz flat optics in 6G and beyond wireless communication devices.

Improving Posyandu Cadres’ Skills to Support Primary Care Integration
abstractText: Posyandu is currently undergoing health-system transformation through the integration of primary care services targeting all stages of the human life cycle, with Posyandu cadres playing a key role in service delivery. Cadre regeneration remains necessary; however, some newly recruited Posyandu cadres have not previously received information or training on Posyandu management. This community service activity was conducted as a training program for newly recruited Posyandu cadres to improve their skills. The participants were 42 newly recruited Posyandu cadres from Kepanjen Kidul Subdistrict, Kepanjen Kidul District, Blitar City. The training was conducted over two days, 22–23 July 2026, by healthcare professionals from Kepanjen Kidul Community Health Center and community service team members from Poltekkes Kemenkes Malang. The classroom-based training included Posyandu management, simulation of effective communication using the SAJI model, and simulation of Posyandu services using the five-step procedure. The results indicated that the cadres had good perceptions and knowledge of Posyandu management and were able to simulate the five-step Posyandu service procedure. The training improved cadres’ knowledge, self-confidence, effective communication skills, and ability to provide Posyandu services. Therefore, training for Posyandu cadres should be conducted regularly.

title: Anti-inflammatory Activity of Clove Oil and Mangosteen Peel Extract on Lipopolysaccharide/UVA+UVB-induced Inflammatory Mediators and Effect on Wound Healing of HaCaT Cells
abstractText: This research examined the anti-inflammatory and wound-healing activity of clove oil and mangosteen peel extract. The clove oil, mangosteen peel, and a combination of clove oil with mangosteen peel extract (1:1) were assessed via modulation of the production of pro-inflammatory molecules by inhibition of the pro-inflammatory cytokines (tumor necrosis factor-α: TNF-α, prostaglandin E2: PGE2) production and the reduction of inflammatory cytokines such as interleukin 10 (IL-10) in the HaCaT cell model. Wound healing activity and cytotoxicity of clove oil and mangosteen peel extract on HaCaT cells were also evaluated. In addition, the combination of clove oil with mangosteen peel extract (1:1) inhibited the production of TNF-α (20.21 ± 0.47 pg/ml) and PGE2 (6.88 ± 0.01 pg/ml) and induced the production of IL-10 (218.44 ± 4.90 pg/ml). The percentage of wound healing (% wound closure) was evident at 48 hours. The combination of clove oil and mangosteen peel extract exhibited complete wound closure with no cytotoxicity. These results provided scientific evidence supporting the efficacy of the combined use of clove oil and mangosteen peel in reducing inflammatory processes.

title: Machine learning surrogates for predicting and interpreting flood fragility parameters of masonry walls
abstractText: Abstract Flood-induced out-of-plane collapse of masonry walls is a recurrent cause of severe building damage and loss during flood events, particularly in low-rise residential construction. Assessing this failure mode at scale remains challenging: simplified fragility models are fast but often lack physical transparency, while mechanics-based analyses are interpretable but computationally expensive. This study develops a mechanics-informed surrogate modelling framework that bridges this gap. Machine-learning surrogates, including linear sparse regressions, kernel-based methods, and ensemble models, are trained on a constrained synthetic dataset generated from a mechanics-based wall collapse formulation. This enables fragility parameters to be predicted with accuracy comparable to the reference simulator while retaining a direct link to the governing structural mechanisms within the adopted modelling domain. A central contribution of the work is the explicit integration of explainable artificial intelligence, allowing the role of geometry, openings, vertical connectivity, and boundary restraint to be quantified and interpreted in physically meaningful terms. The results reveal stable and intuitive collapse drivers across boundary configurations, with the upper-floor contribution, thickness-related descriptors, and boundary restraint forming the dominant sensitivity group, while masonry density and opening-related variables have secondary or model-dependent influence. The consistency of these trends across linear and nonlinear surrogate models demonstrates that the framework captures not only fragility estimates but also mechanically consistent sensitivity patterns of wall overturning. By combining mechanics-based simulations with surrogate modelling, the proposed approach enables efficient and physically interpretable assessment of masonry wall fragility.

A Study on Senior High School English Continuation Writing Teaching Based on Deep Learning
abstractText: First introduced, continuation writing has sparked widespread academic debate. English teachers have embraced this task because it combines reading and writing, two integrated language skills, and helps nurture students’ critical and creative thinking. Even so, most high school English lessons on continuation writing still prioritize surface-level language drills. They pay little attention to textual logic and the shaping of ideas, leaving students reliant on rigid templates and struggling to build coherent plots. True integration of reading and writing thus rarely takes place. Deep learning prioritizes thorough text comprehension, knowledge transfer and critical inquiry. It fits well with the new curriculum standards that target the core competencies of English education. Drawing on deep learning theory, this paper identifies common pitfalls in high school continuation writing instruction. Using the continuation writing prompt from the 2026 National College Entrance Examination Paper II as a case, it develops teaching strategies across four stages: close discourse analysis,collaborative construction, thematic refinement and reflective assessment. These approaches encourage students to unpack the internal logic of the original text, support them to internalize language and produce creative writing, and ultimately cultivate core competencies including linguistic competence and thinking quality.

title: PERFIL EPIDEMIOLÓGICO E TENDÊNCIA TEMPORAL DAS NOTIFICAÇÕES DE VIOLÊNCIA AUTOPROVOCADA E DOS ÓBITOS POR SUICÍDIO ENTRE INDÍGENAS NO TOCANTINS, 2015–2025
abstractText: A violência autoprovocada constitui um problema de saúde pública cuja ocorrência entre povos indígenas demanda atenção às particularidades epidemiológicas, sociais e culturais dessa população. Este estudo teve como objetivo descrever o perfil epidemiológico e a tendência temporal das notificações de violência autoprovocada e dos óbitos por suicídio entre indígenas residentes no Tocantins, no período de 2015 a 2025. Trata-se de um estudo epidemiológico observacional, ecológico, retrospectivo, de série temporal, realizado com dados secundários do Sistema de Informação de Agravos de Notificação (Sinan) e do Sistema de Informações sobre Mortalidade (SIM), disponibilizados pelo Departamento de Informática do Sistema Único de Saúde. O estudo realizou análises descritivas e regressões lineares exploratórias das contagens anuais. O estudo identificou 235 notificações de violência autoprovocada e 47 óbitos por lesões autoprovocadas intencionalmente. As notificações apresentaram distribuição equilibrada entre os sexos, enquanto os homens corresponderam a 76,6% dos óbitos. A faixa etária de 15 a 29 anos concentrou 54,5% das notificações e 68,1% dos óbitos. Observou-se tendência crescente estatisticamente significativa nas contagens anuais de notificações, mas não nos óbitos. O enforcamento, o estrangulamento e a sufocação corresponderam a 89,4% dos óbitos. Os achados evidenciam diferenças entre os perfis da violência notificada e da mortalidade, reforçando a necessidade de aprimorar a vigilância epidemiológica e desenvolver estratégias de prevenção culturalmente adequadas às comunidades indígenas.

title: Zinc ions inhibit migrasome biogenesis and impair platelet function by targeting cholesterol and sphingomyelin
abstractText: Aim: Zinc ions are critical regulators of cellular homeostasis and hemostasis. Migrasomes promote thrombus formation, yet whether zinc ions influence migrasome biogenesis and the associated thrombotic outcomes remains unexplored. This work therefore examined how zinc ions affect migrasome formation and assessed the functional consequences for platelet aggregation and bleeding volume. Methods: We performed RNA sequencing on Huh7.5.1 cells treated with ZnSO4 or zinc gluconate. Migrasome formation was evaluated in both these cells and in mouse whole blood, while intracellular zinc levels were manipulated using disulfiram to enhance efflux or anti-solute carrier family 39 member 6 (SLC39A6) antibodies to inhibit uptake. Migrasomes were visualized through immunofluorescence with wheat germ agglutinin (WGA). Changes in cholesterol, sphingomyelin and reactive oxygen species (ROS) levels in response to zinc ions were measured. Migrasomes were isolated from mouse blood using a specialized isolation kit. Results: Zinc ions treatment reduced migrasome numbers in both cellular and whole-blood models in a dose-dependent manner. Zinc ions also decreased cholesterol, sphingomyelin, and ROS levels and impaired migrasome biogenesis. In mice, zinc administration reduced platelet counts and aggregation while increasing bleeding volume. Conclusion: Our findings demonstrate that zinc ions modulate migrasome formation by lowering cholesterol levels, thereby negatively regulating platelet aggregation. This research enhances the current understanding of trace element biology and suggests that modulating zinc ion levels could be a potential therapeutic strategy for managing hemostatic disorders.

title: Joint latent class mixed model trajectories of estimated glomerular filtration rate related to mortality and physical activity in older adults
abstractText: Abstract Deterioration of renal function occurs with age, leading in many individuals to chronic kidney disease, considerable disability and premature mortality. The trajectories of kidney function decline and potential protective factors remain poorly understood, especially in older individuals. We therefore investigated eGFR-decline trajectories related to mortality as well as the influence of physical activity patterns on trajectory membership in a population-based cohort of older individuals. 1,506 community-dwelling adults aged $$\:\ge\:$$ 65 years were recruited in 2009 and followed up for up to three times. Trajectories of eGFR-decline and their relation with mortality were determined using joint latent class models. The association of physical activity (PA) and sedentary behavior (SB), determined by accelerometer measurements at baseline, with class-membership was studied with logistic regression. There were 2,812 observations on eGFR. We identified two trajectories, one starting with a lower mean baseline eGFR value and showing a stronger decline over time and higher mortality. In adjusted models, we found robust inverse associations of time spent in PA and total steps with being in this trajectory (Odds ratios with 95%-confidence intervals of 0.72 [0.60, 0.87] for 10 min and 0.73 [0.62, 0.86] for 1000 steps); SB was positively associated with this trajectory (2.51 [1.65, 3.81] for 100 min). PA was negatively and SB was positively associated with the worse trajectory. This may indicate that interventions for increasing PA may potentially be viable strategies to prevent impaired renal function and slow age-related functional decline in older individuals and should be investigated in future studies.

title: Exploration of Pathways for Constructing New Liberal Arts Program Clusters in Private Higher Education Institutions from the Perspective of a Digital Rule-of-Law Education Community
abstractText: The digital rule-of-law education community represents a collaborative talent cultivation model involving multiple stakeholders, characterized by symbiotic relationships among participants, interconnectivity of resources, and aligned objectives; it thereby provides a theoretical framework for the development of new liberal arts program clusters in private universities. In this context, the digital rule-of-law education community serves as an external educational ecosystem, while the new liberal arts program cluster functions as an internal implementation vehicle; the two exhibit a deep synergistic relationship, and their coordinated development can enable the supply side of liberal arts education to proactively adapt to the practical demands of digital governance. By advancing the construction of such program clusters, private universities can address regional shortages of digital rule-of-law professionals, overcome the challenge of homogenization among liberal arts programs, and optimize the allocation of limited educational resources. However, several shortcomings persist in current efforts: a lack of top-level strategic planning for digital rule-of-law education; disciplinary barriers that hinder interdisciplinary integration; superficial collaboration among government agencies, enterprises, universities, and research institutions; ambiguous delineation of rights and responsibilities among community participants; and the absence of well-established long-term operational mechanisms. To enhance the quality of these program clusters through the establishment of such communities, it is essential to: refine top-level strategic planning by integrating digital rule-of-law literacy throughout the entire talent cultivation process; dismantle departmental and programmatic barriers by consolidating practical resources to redesign interdisciplinary curricula, thereby facilitating program iteration and upgrading; and establish a robust community governance framework that clarifies the roles and responsibilities of all parties, thereby building a sustainable collaborative talent cultivation system. Addressing the demand for positions in grassroots digital governance, data compliance, and online legal services, private universities should integrate both internal and external educational resources, bridge the gap between classroom instruction and practical application scenarios, and develop operational models for program clusters that align with the distinctive characteristics of private institutions. This approach will cultivate application-oriented new liberal arts professionals who possess humanistic literacy, legal reasoning capabilities, and practical digital competencies, thereby contributing to local digital social governance and the growth of regional digital economies.

title: Employment, property offenses, and homelessness: a quantitative analysis of structural disadvantage and arrest outcomes
abstractText: Abstract The annual Point-in-Time count indicates homelessness in the US increased by 18% between 2023 and 2024. Because this count is completed in January, it does not consider those who are homeless for less than 30 days during other parts of the year. Acute homelessness is intimately connected with mental illness, criminal arrests, and poverty. Employment is a viable means through which persons experiencing homelessness can escape this cycle. Utilizing the 2016 Survey of Prison Inmates as data and General Strain Theory as an interpretive lens, this study examines the extent to which different types of acute homelessness impact property offense arrests and the moderating role of employment. Respondents who were living in a vehicle 30 days before their arrest had significantly greater odds of being arrested for a property offense at 85% (OR = 1.85, 95% CI [1.34, 2.55]). Those living in a shelter or on the streets had significantly higher odds at 156% (OR = 2.56, 95% CI [1.95, 3.36]) of being arrested for a property offense. Among respondents who were living in a car 30 days before their arrest, being employed significantly reduced the odds of committing a property offense by 41% (OR = 0.59, 95% CI [0.36, 0.96]). The findings provide evidence that acute homelessness is associated with increased property offending, and employment moderates this association, consistent with GST. Our interaction finding that employment significantly reduced property offense odds among vehicle-dwelling individuals points toward economic integration as a more effective lever than enforcement.

title: ATUAÇÃO DA ENFERMAGEM FRENTE À SÍNDROME DE BURNOUT: FATORES DE RISCO E ESTRATÉGIAS DE PREVENÇÃO NO AMBIENTE HOSPITALAR: UMA REVISÃO INTEGRATIVA DA LITERATURA
abstractText: A Síndrome de Burnout constitui importante problema de saúde ocupacional entre profissionais de enfermagem, especialmente no ambiente hospitalar. Este artigo objetiva analisar a atuação da enfermagem frente ao Burnout, identificando fatores de risco e estratégias de prevenção. Trata-se de revisão literária, qualitativa, descritiva e exploratória, fundamentada em produções científicas sobre a temática. Os resultados evidenciam que sobrecarga laboral, jornadas prolongadas, déficit de profissionais, pressão por produtividade, conflitos interpessoais e fatores emocionais favorecem o esgotamento profissional. Conclui-se que apoio emocional, valorização profissional e melhoria das condições de trabalho são estratégias fundamentais para prevenir o Burnout e promover qualidade assistencial na enfermagem hospitalar.

title: Awareness of canned-food hazards and reported canned-food practices among health-science undergraduates at a university in south-western Nigeria: a cross-sectional study
abstractText: Abstract Background Canned foods are widely used in Nigeria, but little is known about how well consumers recognise canned-food-specific hazards or how they handle opened cans. We describe responses to individual questionnaire items on canned-food hazards, labelling and handling among undergraduates of a health-science college in south-western Nigeria. Methods This cross-sectional survey was conducted between January and March 2018 among 200 undergraduates of the Obafemi Awolowo College of Health Sciences, Olabisi Onabanjo University, drawn from a sampling frame of 2,613 students by proportionate stratified allocation across classes and systematic random selection within classes. A self-administered questionnaire with 30 items was used. Results are reported item by item with Wilson 95% confidence intervals (CI). Associations of sex, age and marital status with selected practices were explored with Fisher’s exact or Monte Carlo exact tests, with effect sizes and Holm adjustment across eight tests. No composite knowledge score is reported because the scoring rule cannot be verified. Results Mean age was 21.0 ± 1.7 years and 55.0% were female. Food in a dented can was correctly judged unsafe by 55.5% (95% CI 48.6–62.2); 18.5% judged it safe and 26.0% were unsure. Only 31.5% (25.5–38.2) affirmed that botulism can follow canned-food consumption (an item that did not specify improper processing). Most (85.5%; 80.0–89.7) recognised that canned foods are high in salt, and 44.0% (37.3–50.9) selected the keyed answer to a label-content item. Overall, 67.5% (60.7–73.6) reported checking expiry dates (78.9% of the 171 who answered yes or no; 29 chose “no response”). 61% (54.1–67.5) retained part of an opened can; where and how it was stored was asked in a free-text item that could not be analysed, so retention cannot be classed as unsafe. Women more often reported that nutrition information influenced purchase (79.1% versus 56.7%; odds ratio 2.89, 1.56–5.38; Holm-adjusted p = 0.006). Other associations were weak or not robust to multiple testing. Conclusions In this single-college sample surveyed in 2018, recognition of canned-food-specific hazards was uneven, and several practices could not be classed as safe or unsafe with the data collected. The instrument did not measure attitudes towards food safety. Findings are exploratory and cannot be generalised to other students or to current behaviour. Larger multi-site studies with a validated instrument, measured storage conditions and current data are needed to guide education on can inspection, post-opening storage and label literacy.

title: The protection of chronic cerebral ischemia by Hua-Feng-Dan involves the modulation of hippocampal transcriptome and gut dysbiosis
abstractText: Abstract The protective effects of Hua-Feng-Dan recipes against chronic cerebral hypoperfusion-induced ischemia were examined; RNA-seq and 16 S-rRNA-seq were used to explore the molecular mechanisms. Male Sprague-Dawley rats underwent unilateral common carotid artery ligation surgery to establish chronic cerebral hypoperfusion (CCH) models. Then, the CCH rats were treated with various Hua-Feng-Dan recipes in diet for 20 days. Finally, behavioral tests were performed, followed by histopathology. Hippocampal RNA was isolated for RNA-seq and RT-qPCR analyses; Colon bacterial DNA was isolated for 16 S rRNA-seq and bioinformatics. The CCH rats exhibited cognition deficits evidenced by Behavioral tests. The neurons in the hippocampus CA1 area were damaged. Hua-Feng-Dan recipes as Reduced_H (0.5 g/kg), Original, and Nonferment improved behavioral deficits and morphological changes, while Reduced_L (0.25 g/kg) was ineffective. RNA-seq revealed distinct gene expression pattern among groups. Ingenuity pathway analysis of differentially expressed genes revealed Hua-Feng-Dan recipes ameliorated Canonical pathways involved in cytosolic Ca 2+ overload, disruption of IGF homeostasis and Neutrophil degranulation; attenuated CCH-activated Upstream regulators such as IL1B, IL6, TNF, IGF1, and glucose metabolism. CCH-decreased Firmicutes/Bacteroidetes ratio were recovered by Hua-Feng-Dan recipes. CCH-increased Prevotellaceae and decreased Lachnospiraceae were attenuated; CCH-increased ASV1 and decreased ASV39 were brought to normal after Hua-Feng-Dan treatments. Similar to the efficacy against CCH, Reduced_L was ineffective in transcriptome and gut microbiota analysis. Hua-Feng-Dan recipes (Reduced_H, Original, and Nonferment) are effective against CCH-induced chronic cerebral ischemia, while Reduced_L was ineffective. The mechanisms of the protection are related to transcriptome regulation in the hippocampus, and modulation of CCH-disrupted gut dysbiosis.

title: Construction, editorial practice, and AI-assisted evaluation of the Chinese Medical Research Reporting Specification Checklist System
PENERAPAN JURNAL INVESTIGASI BERBASIS PENDEKATAN MULTIMODAL UNTUK MENDORONG PARTISIPASI MURID DALAM PEMBELAJARAN HIKAYAT KELAS X
abstractText: Partisipasi murid dalam pembelajaran hikayat kerap dibaca sebatas keberanian berbicara sehingga keterlibatan melalui tindakan belajar kurang terpetakan. Penelitian ini bertujuan mendeskripsikan perubahan partisipasi murid kelas X-2 SMAN 7 Cirebon sebelum dan sesudah penerapan Jurnal Investigasi berbasis pendekatan multimodal. Penelitian menggunakan pendekatan kuantitatif dengan desain pra-eksperimen one-group pretest-posttest pada 38 murid. Partisipasi diamati melalui lembar observasi 12 indikator dalam empat dimensi, dengan tiga indikator berbasis tuturan dan sembilan berbasis tindakan, menggunakan skala 1–4. Data dianalisis secara deskriptif, sedangkan uji Wilcoxon digunakan sebagai analisis inferensial pendukung. Rerata skor partisipasi meningkat dari 1,92 (48,08%; kategori rendah) menjadi 2,74 (68,59%; kategori tinggi). N-Gain yang dilaporkan sebesar 0,39 (kategori sedang), tetapi ditafsirkan sebagai ukuran deskriptif eksploratif karena skor berasal dari observasi ordinal. Sebanyak 31 dari 38 murid mengalami peningkatan skor, sedangkan 11 murid memiliki N-Gain rendah. Menanggapi gagasan teman secara lisan tetap menjadi indikator terendah. Karena penelitian tidak menggunakan kelompok pembanding dan pengamatan dilakukan oleh satu orang, hasil tidak dapat disimpulkan sebagai pengaruh kausal perlakuan. Temuan ini memberikan gambaran awal yang perlu diuji melalui pengukuran yang lebih setara dan reliabel.

title: Family-Based Tuberculosis Prevention Through Self-Management Education (SME) for Community Health Workers in Rural East Indonesia
abstractText: Pulmonary Tuberculosis (TB) remains a significant public health concern in Indonesia, especially in East Nusa Tenggara Province. This community service program aimed to strengthen the knowledge and skills of community health workers (cadres) in delivering family-based TB prevention through a Self-Management Education (SME) approach. A pre–post descriptive design was implemented involving 35 active Integrated Service Post (ISP) health cadres in Manusak Village, Kupang Regency. The intervention included cadres training, developing and distributing educational materials (modules, posters, and leaflets), conducting structured home visits, and implementing monitoring tools. Cadres’ knowledge and skills were measured using a structured 15-item questionnaire and a skills observational checklist before and after the intervention. The results showed an increase in average knowledge scores from 57% before the intervention to 94% after the intervention. Cadres’ skills also improved markedly, with the proportion of cadres categorized as having good skills increasing from 6% at baseline to 94% after the intervention. This program demonstrates that SME is a feasible and effective approach to empowering community health cadres to deliver family-based TB prevention in rural settings. Each family affected by TB received four home visits over an eight-week period. Post-intervention observations indicated that 80% of families practiced proper cough etiquette, 72% maintained adequate household ventilation and 64% consistently wore masks when interacting with TB patients. These results reflect an improvement in household-level TB preventive behaviors. Longitudinal follow-up is recommended to assess whether cadres continue to apply SME principles consistently, and whether preventive behaviors among families are maintained over time.

title: Assessment of sleep quality using the pittsburgh sleep quality index (psqi) in patients after cardiac surgery at Hanoi Heart Hospital
abstractText: Background & Objectives: Sleep disturbances are prevalent yet frequently overlooked functional complications in cardiac surgery patients. This study aimed to describe sleep characteristics and assess sleep quality using the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI) in post-cardiac surgery patients at Hanoi Heart Hospital. Methods: A cross-sectional descriptive study was conducted on 71 elective post-cardiac surgery patients at Hanoi Heart Hospital from August 1, 2024, to February 28, 2025. Sleep quality was evaluated using the PSQI questionnaire, alongside assessments of postoperative pain (Visual Analogue Scale - VAS) and anxiety (Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale - Anxiety subscale - HADS-A). Results: The overall prevalence of poor sleep quality (global PSQI score > 5) was 69.01%, including 33.80% mild, 28.17% moderate, and 5.63% severe sleep disturbance. The median global PSQI score was 9.0 (interquartile range: 4.0 – 12.0). Regarding specific components: 36.62% of patients had actual nocturnal sleep duration < 5 hours (mean: 5.45 ± 2.12 hours); 36.62% experienced prolonged sleep latency > 30 minutes (median: 30 minutes); 45.07% exhibited severely impaired sleep efficiency (< 65%) with a median sleep efficiency of 67.0% (IQR: 50.0% – 89.0%). Only 5.63% used sleep medications, and 85.92% reported minimal daytime dysfunction. Conclusion: Poor sleep quality is highly prevalent (69.01%) among post-cardiac surgery patients, characterized by truncated sleep duration, prolonged sleep latency, and compromised sleep efficiency. Routine screening protocols and structured multi-modal sleep-promoting nursing interventions should be systematically integrated into Enhanced Recovery After Cardiac Surgery (ERAS Cardiac) pathways.

Creative Industries in Ivanovo Oblast: Traditions and Challenges in Introducing Innovations
abstractText: This article examines creative industries in Ivanovo Oblast, focusing on the city of Shuya and Yuryevets District. The relevance of the study stems from the formal recognition of creative industries in federal legislation and the need to identify practical approaches to their development in small and medium-sized towns in an industrial region with a long-established textile specialization. Particular attention is paid to how the interplay of historical and cultural heritage, local brands, and new forms of entrepreneurship influences the transformation of the economic and sociocultural landscape of the region. The aim of the study is to demonstrate the specific features of the formation and operation of creative industries in Ivanovo Oblast, drawing on the typology established in Article 6 of the Federal Law “On the Development of Creative Industries in the Russian Federation.” The study focuses on craft and gastronomic practices, local brands, and creative communities in Shuya and Yuryevets District. Its objectives include analyzing key stakeholders, forms of cooperation, and barriers to the development of the creative sector in small towns. The empirical basis consists of materials from projects conducted by the Center for Small Town Research and the Center for Territorial Development, an autonomous nonprofit organization; findings from field expeditions, observations, and interviews with business representatives and local communities; and data from regional media and publicly available online sources. Methodologically, the study combines statistical and documentary analysis with field research, including participatory design, expert discussions held as part of the Third Forum “Small Towns—New Territories for Creative Industries,” and the piloting of formats for the Labaz urban living room. The findings indicate that the introduction of innovations remains unsystematic. Craftspeople and small business owners need greater support through local legislative initiatives. The creative industries sector is characterized by a diversity of organizational and economic forms, as well as the phenomena of “dispersed workshops” and “dispersed crafts.” The study identifies key gaps in institutional support, particularly with regard to the legal status of craftspeople, sales infrastructure, and taxation arrangements. Targeted initiatives—from the local brands Shuyskie Sittsy and Shuyskoe Vedro to agritourism projects in Yuryevets District—offer an alternative development pathway for local economies. However, these initiatives require a targeted regional policy that includes the establishment of a register of craftspeople and the relaxation of excessive regulatory requirements. The article is intended for researchers in the creative economy, specialists in regional and municipal policy, and territorial development practitioners working with small towns and rural areas.

Effects of recycled PET aggregate size and replacement level on hot mix asphalt performance
abstractText: Abstract The increasing accumulation of plastic waste has intensified the need for sustainable reuse strategies in construction materials. This study investigates the feasibility of using recycled polyethylene terephthalate (rPET) from post‑consumer bottles as a partial replacement for natural aggregates in hot mix asphalt (HMA) using the dry mixing method, emphasizing the influence of particle size and replacement level on HMA performance. rPET particles with natural‑aggregate‑like physical characteristics were produced and sieved into standard size fractions to function as rPET aggregates. The adhesion behavior and mechanical properties of rPET aggregates were evaluated and compared with limestone aggregates used in this study under different temperature conditions. HMA performance was assessed through dynamic creep tests (flow number and permanent deformation) at 40 °C, and moisture susceptibility and indirect tensile fatigue tests at 25 °C. To investigate the effect of particle size, 10% of natural aggregates (by volume) were replaced with rPET aggregates in five size ranges from ≤ 0.3 to 19 mm, and the most effective range was used to determine the optimum replacement level. The results showed that at medium-to-high temperatures, rPET had better interfacial adhesion with bitumen than with limestone, and rPET aggregates performed better in the LAA and AIV tests. Optimal performance was achieved using 4.75–12.5 mm rPET aggregates, where 18% replacement increased creep resistance by 57% and reduced moisture susceptibility by 7%, while 16% replacement improved fatigue life by 295%. These findings demonstrate that rPET aggregates provide an environmentally sustainable alternative for enhancing HMA performance.

title: The Relationship Between Family Cultural Practices and Childbirth Behavior in Cikunir Village Tasikmalaya Regency
abstractText: Background: Family cultural practices may influence decision-making and mothers' behavior in seeking childbirth assistance. Beliefs about the roles of husbands or family members, inherited cultural advice, perceptions of health-service costs, and acceptance of referral may affect childbirth-related decisions. This study examined the relationship between family cultural practices and childbirth behavior in Cikunir Village, Tasikmalaya Regency. Objective: To describe family cultural practices and analyze their relationship with childbirth behavior among postpartum mothers in Cikunir Village, Tasikmalaya Regency. Methods: This quantitative analytical observational study used a cross-sectional design. The population comprised postpartum mothers in Cikunir Village, and the sample included 22 mothers who were 1–2 months postpartum. Total sampling was used, including all eligible members of the population. Results: In the group with less-supportive cultural practices, 3 mothers (37.5%) had good childbirth behavior, while 5 (62.5%) had moderate/poor behavior. In the group with moderately supportive/supportive practices, 5 mothers (35.7%) had good behavior and 9 (64.3%) had moderate/poor behavior. Fisher's exact test yielded p = 1.000 (p > 0.05), OR = 1.08, and 95% CI = 0.18–6.54, indicating no statistically significant relationship. Conclusion: Family cultural practices remain evident among postpartum mothers in Cikunir Village, particularly in family decision-making, cultural advice, perceptions of health services, and attitudes toward medical referral. Midwives should provide culturally sensitive education and birth preparedness and involve husbands and families in decision-making. Limitations: The small sample (22 respondents) and the study's restriction to one village limit generalizability. The cross-sectional design cannot establish causality. Future studies should include larger samples and wider geographic coverage to provide stronger empirical evidence.

title: Comparison of three occlusal splint material systems manufactured by conventional, subtractive, and additive techniques
abstractText: Abstract Objectives To compare the thermal–viscoelastic behavior, hygroscopic properties, color stability, and surface morphology of three commercial occlusal splint material systems produced by conventional heat polymerization, CAD/CAM milling, and 3D printing. The null hypothesis was that the three material systems would not differ in thermal-viscoelastic behavior, hygroscopic properties, or color stability. Surface morphology was assessed qualitatively as a complementary outcome. Materials and methods Heat-polymerized polymethyl methacrylate (HEC), CAD/CAM-milled polymethyl methacrylate (CAD-M), and a 3D-printed photopolymer resin (3DP) were evaluated. Dynamic mechanical analysis was performed to determine glass transition temperature (Tg), tan δ, and thermal heterogeneity ( n = 5). Water sorption (WS), solubility (SL), and color change after coffee immersion (ΔE00) were assessed ( n = 8). Surface morphology was qualitatively analyzed by atomic force microscopy and scanning electron microscopy. Results Significant differences were observed among the material systems for thermal and hygroscopic outcomes. CAD-M presented the highest mean Tg (149.58 ± 0.95 °C), the lowest water sorption (18.76 ± 0.56 µg/mm³), the lowest solubility (2.59 ± 0.48 µg/mm³), and a ΔE00 of 2.29 ± 1.20 after 7 days of coffee immersion. Conversely, 3DP showed the lowest Tg (83.18 ± 7.87 °C), highest WS (35.12 ± 0.82 µg/mm³), highest SL (6.16 ± 0.40 µg/mm³), greatest color change, and a more irregular surface morphology. Conclusions The three evaluated commercial material systems differed in thermal-viscoelastic behavior, hygroscopic properties, color stability, and surface morphology. Among the specific systems tested, CAD-M showed the most favorable overall laboratory profile. Because each manufacturing approach was represented by a single commercial material with a distinct composition, these differences cannot be attributed exclusively to the manufacturing route. Clinical relevance Under the in vitro conditions tested, the milled material system showed a higher glass transition temperature and lower water sorption, solubility and coffee-induced discoloration than the 3D-printed system. Whether these laboratory differences translate into differences in the clinical performance of occlusal splints was not assessed in this study.

title: Assessing transit-oriented development potential in Egypt’s emerging LRT corridor: a node–place assessment within a 3Vs- and SDG-aligned framework
abstractText: Abstract Integrating transportation and land-use planning is essential for promoting sustainable urban development, particularly in rapidly expanding metropolitan regions. Transit-Oriented Development (TOD) provides a planning approach for concentrating compact, mixed-use, and pedestrian-oriented development around public transport stations. However, TOD strategies cannot be applied uniformly across a transit corridor because station areas differ in their network roles, built environments, development stages, and market conditions. This study proposes a 3Vs- and Sustainable Development Goal (SDG)-aligned framework for assessing station-level TOD potential and applies its currently measurable dimensions to Egypt’s emerging Light Rail Transit corridor connecting El Salam, the New Administrative Capital, and 10th of Ramadan City. The empirical application evaluates selected stations through Node and Place indicators using transit-network information, ridership data, land-use analysis, street-network assessment, and GIS-based spatial analysis. Market Value is retained within the conceptual framework but is not quantitatively assessed because several station areas remain under development and lack stable and comparable population, employment, and real-estate-market data. The results reveal substantial differences among the selected stations. Adly Mansour demonstrates the strongest combination of transport connectivity and local accessibility, while stations in emerging urban areas exhibit more moderate Node and Place conditions that require gradual and context-sensitive interventions. The study provides preliminary development directions for station areas and demonstrates how a staged Node–Place assessment can support TOD planning while remaining aligned with broader sustainability and SDG priorities. Future longitudinal assessment is required to incorporate Market Value as the surrounding urban areas mature. A concise robustness check further showed that the relative ordering of the four stations with complete indicator coverage remained unchanged under alternative normalization procedures and moderate weighting perturbations.

Artificial Intelligence Framework Predicts Residual Ecotoxicity During Advanced Oxidation Water Treatment
abstractText: General Background Advanced oxidation processes (AOPs) efficiently degrade structurally resistant contaminants of emerging concern (CECs) in tertiary wastewater treatment. Specific Background Conventional performance metrics rely on the disappearance of the parent compound, ignoring the formation of transformation products (TPs) whose persistence, mobility, and toxicity often exceed those of the parent structure. Knowledge Gap Current targeted analytical workflows frequently leave transient TPs undetected, and existing predictive models lack a cohesive, validated framework that integrates radical reactivity, in silico enumeration, and toxicity predictions to actively manage residual risk. Aims This critical review evaluates the mechanistic origins of toxic TPs and proposes a conceptual tiered framework that couples density functional theory (DFT) reactivity descriptors, graph neural networks (GNNs), high-resolution mass spectrometry (HRMS), and machine-learning toxicity predictions into a mixture-aware Net Ecotoxicity Index (NEI). Results Radical-mediated electrophilic addition, single-electron transfer, and hydrogen abstraction generate reactive electrophiles and halogenated or nitrated TPs that significantly raise residual mixture toxicity. The proposed AI-assisted framework integrates these chemical pathways to predict TP formation and structure, prioritizing analytical screening through HRMS, and subsequently assessing ecotoxicity using QSAR models to inform supervisory oxidant dosing. Novelty This framework shifts the AOP control paradigm from parent-compound degradation tracking to prospective, AI-driven residual ecotoxicity prediction and mitigation. Implications Adopting mixture-aware predictive control strategies requires establishing open TP datasets, applying precise applicability domains in modeling, and shifting regulatory targets toward effect-based risk assessments. Highlights: Evaluating advanced oxidation performance solely by parent compound degradation masks the potential toxicity of transformation products. Integrating DFT descriptors and graph neural networks enables the prospective in silico identification of toxic transformation products. AI-assisted toxicity predictions integrated with HRMS screening can dynamically control oxidant dosing to minimize residual ecotoxicity. Keywords: Advanced Oxidation Processes, Residual Ecotoxicity, Transformation Products, Machine Learning, Net Ecotoxicity Index

Atomistic understanding of hybrid bonding in Cu interfaces using multiscale microscopy
abstractText: Achieving wafer-scale reliability in Cu–Cu hybrid bonding remains challenging due to process-induced non-uniformities and the limited understanding of buried interfacial contamination. Here, we employ a correlative multiscale microscopy framework combining scanning electron microscopy, transmission electron microscopy, and atom probe tomography (APT) to investigate bond degradation from the wafer center to the edge. We observe progressive bond deterioration characterized by interfacial delamination, reduced Cu grain size, and the formation of a nanometer-scale amorphous interlayer. While such interlayers have been widely observed in hybrid bonding, their chemical nature has remained largely unresolved. APT directly reveals that the interlayer consists of Si-, C-, and N-bearing species consistent with contributions from the adjacent SiCN dielectric, together with Cu oxide and organic-related contaminants. By correlating interlayer chemistry and thickness with microstructural evolution, we establish a direct link between interfacial contamination, suppressed cross-interface grain growth, and bond degradation. Furthermore, we observe a progressive thickness-dependent degradation, where interfacial thickening from ∼1 to 2 nm at the center to ∼2 to 3 nm in the donut region is accompanied by deterioration in mechanical bond integrity and localized delamination. These findings provide atomistic insight into the chemistry governing hybrid bond reliability and establish quantitative guidelines for process optimization toward wafer-scale integration.

title: Content Validity of a Framework for Problem-Solving Competence in Programming Among Information Technology Students: A Two-Round Delphi Study in Vietnam
abstractText: Competence-based education requires that learning outcomes for information technology (IT) programs rest on a competence framework whose content has been validated by experts, yet Vietnam has no framework for problem-solving competence in programming validated through a quantitative, criterion-based procedure. This study validated the content of such a framework, comprising five competence components, twenty-one criteria, and behavioural indicators across four developmental levels, using a two-round Delphi procedure with a purposively heterogeneous, Vietnam-based panel of 23 experts drawn from programming instruction, the software industry, and educational measurement. Round 1 (21 respondents; 91.3%) elicited structured qualitative judgements that generated six documented revisions. Round 2, sent to the same fixed panel (n = 20; 87.0%; 19 also responding in Round 1), rated 169 items against three consensus criteria set in advance: an item-level content validity index (I-CVI) of at least 0.78, a median of at least 4, and an interquartile range of at most 1. Every one of the 169 items satisfied all three criteria simultaneously, the scale-level index (S-CVI/Ave) reached 0.98, and the predefined stopping rule was therefore met after two rounds; a sensitivity analysis restricted to respondents who passed an embedded attention check left this conclusion unchanged. The validated core comprises twenty-one criteria and eighty-four indicators. Two content areas that experts raised without prompting, collaboration with generative artificial intelligence and exception handling, were integrated as twelve extended indicators at the indicator layer rather than as new criteria, preserving the validated criterion structure; these twelve await separate validation. The framework supplies an evidence-based foundation for writing learning outcomes, constructing analytic rubrics, and designing project-based instruction in IT programmes.

title: AI-assisted diagnostics in male infertility: morphological assessment, molecular stratification, and the translational gap between laboratory performance and clinical utility
abstractText: Abstract Background Male infertility contributes to approximately half of all cases of couple infertility worldwide, yet its diagnostic cornerstone, conventional semen analysis anchored in World Health Organization (WHO) criteria, suffers from inter-observer variability that can reach 30–40% for morphological parameters even among trained andrologists. Computer-assisted sperm analysis (CASA) reduced some sources of error but failed to eliminate the subjectivity inherent in morphological classification, particularly for the acrosome, midpiece, and cytoplasmic droplet defect categories. Convolutional neural networks and ensemble deep learning architectures have since demonstrated high classification accuracy on selected benchmark datasets (detailed under Results), prompting fundamental questions about the clinical readiness and translational utility of AI-assisted andrology. Methods (Approach) This is a critical review that synthesises evidence from peer-reviewed studies identified through targeted searches of PubMed, Scopus, and IEEE Xplore (through May 2025), covering AI applications in sperm morphology classification, motility analysis, non-obstructive azoospermia (NOA) outcome prediction, and sperm selection for intracytoplasmic sperm injection (ICSI), supplemented by hand-searching the reference lists of key articles. Search terms combined controlled vocabulary and free-text terms for “sperm morphology,” “deep learning,” “convolutional neural network,” “azoospermia,” “testicular sperm extraction,” and “ICSI,” restricted to English-language, peer-reviewed publications. Studies were selected for methodological relevance, recency, and clinical significance rather than through a pre-registered, reproducible systematic protocol; no formal risk-of-bias or quality-appraisal instrument (e.g., QUADAS-2 or PROBAST) was applied. This is a deliberate scope decision, declared here rather than implied: the review is a critical, evidence-synthesising appraisal of a fast-moving field, not a systematic or scoping review, and quantitative performance figures drawn from heterogeneous studies (summarised in Table 1) should be read as illustrative of the state of the field rather than as directly comparable, pooled estimates. Results Deep learning models, including ensemble and attention-augmented convolutional architectures, have reported accuracies of 94% to 96.77% and F1-scores of up to 98.2% for sperm morphology classification, principally on the HuSHeM benchmark dataset; the morphology-classification studies summarised in Table 1 report accuracy, precision, or F1-score rather than AUC (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve). Machine learning models integrating hormonal, genetic, and histopathological features achieve AUC values of 0.807 to above 0.90 for predicting sperm retrieval success in microdissection testicular sperm extraction (m-TESE). For AI-assisted real-time sperm selection during ICSI, a prospective sibling-oocyte study of 646 metaphase II oocytes found only a non-significant trend towards improved fertilisation, whereas a separate, smaller sibling-oocyte comparison, reported to date only as a conference abstract, described a statistically significant improvement in fertilisation; live birth rate data remain scarce. However, the predominance of single-centre, algorithmically homogeneous training datasets, absence of prospective multicentre validation, and the opaque decision logic of most deployed models collectively constrain clinical adoption. Conclusions AI-assisted sperm morphology assessment has attained technical maturity but not clinical readiness. The transition from benchmark accuracy to actionable diagnostic utility requires prospective multicentre validation using clinically diverse and ethnically representative cohorts, live birth rate pre-specified as the primary endpoint, with fertilisation and blastulation rates as secondary endpoints, and the development of explainable AI frameworks compatible with regulatory standards including the EU AI Act. The Middle East and North Africa region, characterised by high rates of male-factor infertility, distinct genetic aetiologies, and constrained laboratory infrastructure, represents both a critical validation environment and an equity-relevant deployment target for these technologies.

title: Mapping Climate and Air Quality Risks for Acute Respiratory Infections in Eastern Priangan, Indonesia
abstractText: Climate change has become a significant public health concern, particularly through its influence on air quality and the incidence of respiratory diseases. Variations in temperature, precipitation, humidity, and wind speed have been shown to exacerbate health vulnerabilities, especially in climate-sensitive regions. This study examines the relationship between climatic parameters, air quality, and respiratory disease admissions in East Priangan, Indonesia, using observational data from 2022 to 2023. Findings reveal a distinct increase in respiratory infections during periods of climatic extremes—specifically, high rainfall and temperature during September–November (SON) 2022, and low rainfall and temperature from July to October 2023. Although air quality in the region generally meets national standards, the Air Quality Index (AQI) deteriorated during prolonged dry periods, correlating with a rise in hospital admissions for respiratory illness. Children were identified as the most affected age group, emphasizing the demographic sensitivity to environmental change. These findings highlight the multifactorial nature of respiratory disease risks, shaped by both direct and indirect effects of climate variability. The study recommends integrated mitigation strategies that combine engineering measures, healthcare preparedness, and local government action to address future climate-related health risks.

Assessment of nutrients and material transport in the main tributaries of the Bahía Blanca Estuary (Argentina) and its relationships with hydrologic dynamics and land use
abstractText: Context Land-based activities within a river basin alter nutrient and particle transport, affecting estuarine water quality and ecological health. Aim To assess spatial and seasonal dynamics of nutrients, particulate materials, and physicochemical parameters in Sauce Chico River (SCR), Napostá Grande Stream (NGS) and inner Bahía Blanca Estuary (BBE, Argentina) from autumn 2017 to summer 2018. Methods We analysed 14 sites located in freshwater bodies and within the estuary. Flows, pH, temperature, salinity, turbidity, ammonium (NH4⁺), chlorophyll a (Chl-a), phaeopigments (Phaeo), particulate organic carbon (POC) and suspended particulate matter (SPM) were determined. Key results Average flow rates reflected rainfall patterns. SCR acts as the primary driver of physical sedimentation, transporting significantly more SPM (3492 Mg year−1) than NGS. NGS exerted a stronger chemical influence, with sewage discharges triggering critical NH4+ spikes. Wide POC:Chl-a ratio range in BBE (94–595) and winter POC peaks from the NGS indicate seasonal shifts between terrestrial inputs and estuarine productivity. Conclusions BBE is subjected to dual, tributary-specific stressors – sediment loads from the SCR and nutrient pollution specially from the NGS. Implications Protecting of vulnerable ecosystems, as BBE, requires distinct, integrated watershed management strategies tailored to the unique anthropogenic pressures of each tributary.

title: PETA DESKRIPSI INTERAKTIF BERBASIS THINK-TALK-WRITE DALAM PENGEMBANGAN IDE MENULIS TEKS DESKRIPSI MURID KELAS VII SMP
abstractText: Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk mengetahui kemampuan murid kelas VII-J SMPN 7 Kota Cirebon dalam mengembangkan ide menulis teks deskripsi menggunakan media peta deskripsi interaktif yang dipadukan dengan model pembelajaran Think-Talk-Write (TTW). Pendekatan penelitian yang digunakan adalah kuantitatif dengan metode deskriptif pada sebanyak 30 murid. Data kemampuan menulis diperoleh melalui tugas pre-test dan post-test. Data proses dikumpulkan melalui lembar observasi selama tahapan TTW. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan adanya peningkatan kemampuan menulis murid yang nyata. Hal ini terlihat dari kenaikan nilai rata-rata keseluruhan dari 44,17 pada pre-test menjadi 87,50 pada post-test, dengan N-Gain rata-rata 0,78 (kategori tinggi). Peningkatan terbesar terjadi pada aspek struktur teks.Sebanyak 93,33% murid mencapai kategori baik dan sangat baik. Didukung dengan nilai hasil observasi sebesar 76,67. Media peta deskripsi interaktif dapat digunakan sebagai alternatif kerangka berpikir (scaffolding) visual yang memandu murid menemukan kata kunci pengamatan, berdiskusi, hingga merangkai paragraf secara mandiri. Penelitian ini menyimpulkan bahwa peta deskripsi interaktif dapat digunakan sebagai media terstruktur untuk membantu memecahkan permasalahan pengembangan ide menulis di sekolah menengah. title: Aktivitas Antimikroba In Vitro dari Lactobacillus plantarum terhadap Escherichia coli
abstractText: Latar Belakang: Escherichia coli merupakan bakteri oportunistik yang dapat menyebabkan infeksi, sedangkan Lactobacillus plantarum berpotensi menghasilkan metabolit antimikroba. Tujuan: Mengevaluasi aktivitas antimikroba Lactobacillus plantarum terhadap Escherichia coli secara in vitro. Metode: Penelitian eksperimental laboratorium dengan rancangan post-test only control group design menggunakan kontrol positif (ciprofloxacin), kontrol negatif (blank disc), serta konsentrasi 25%, 50%, dan 75% dengan lima pengulangan tiap kelompok. Analisis dilakukan menggunakan Shapiro–Wilk, Levene, Kruskal–Wallis, dan perbandingan berpasangan dengan koreksi Bonferroni. Hasil: Rerata diameter yang dicatat secara berurutan sebesar 32,80 ± 0,63; 6,00 ± 0,00; 6,00 ± 0,00; 4,49 ± 1,64; dan 9,16 ± 0,38 mm. Terdapat perbedaan antar kelompok (H = 22,607; p < 0,001). Perbedaan signifikan ditemukan pada pasangan K4–K5, K4–K1, K2–K1, dan K3–K1. Kesimpulan: Konsentrasi 75% menunjukkan rerata diameter terbesar di antara tiga kelompok uji, tetapi hasil perlu ditafsirkan dengan mempertimbangkan konsistensi pencatatan diameter cakram dan zona hambat.

title: COMPORTAMENTO TEMPORAL E FATORES ASSOCIADOS ÀS CESARIANAS EM AÇAILÂNDIA-MA: 2015 - 2024
abstractText: Introdução: A cesariana é uma importante intervenção obstétrica quando indicada clinicamente. No entanto, o aumento expressivo de sua realização no Brasil tem gerado preocupação devido aos possíveis impactos maternos, neonatais e econômicos. Nesse contexto, o monitoramento dos indicadores obstétricos é fundamental para compreender o perfil dos partos e subsidiar ações em saúde. Em municípios do interior maranhense, como Açailândia-MA, ainda são escassos os estudos que investigam essa realidade. Objetivo: Analisar o comportamento temporal das cesarianas e descrever as características sociodemográficas, obstétricas e assistenciais dos partos ocorridos em Açailândia-MA entre 2015 e 2024. Metodologia: Estudo epidemiológico, observacional, retrospectivo e descritivo, com abordagem quantitativa. Foram analisados dados do Sistema de Informações sobre Nascidos Vivos (SINASC/DATASUS) referentes aos partos hospitalares ocorridos em Açailândia-MA entre 2015 e 2024. Resultados: Foram registrados 16.453 partos hospitalares, dos quais 8.294 (50,4%) ocorreram por cesariana. Observou-se predominância da via cesárea na maior parte da série histórica. As cesarianas foram mais frequentes entre mulheres com maior idade, maior escolaridade, casadas ou em união consensual, pertencentes ao grupo G5 da Classificação de Robson e com pré-natal adequado ou mais que adequado. A maioria dos recém-nascidos apresentou índice de Apgar satisfatório no primeiro e no quinto minuto de vida. Conclusão: A taxa de cesarianas observada em Açailândia-MA foi superior à recomendada pela Organização Mundial da Saúde. Os resultados evidenciam a necessidade de monitoramento contínuo dos indicadores obstétricos e do fortalecimento de estratégias que promovam o parto vaginal quando clinicamente indicado.

title: Effective Pest Management and Biodiversity Conservation in Bangladesh
abstractText: In Bangladesh, rich agro-biodiversity is increasingly threatened by unsustainable pest management practices, environmental degradation, pest resistance, decline of beneficial species, and contamination of food and water. This study evaluates prevailing pest management strategies, their ecological and economic impacts, and opportunities to develop biodiversity- and eco-friendly pest control systems. A cross-sectional mixed-methods approach was applied across five agroecological zones, involving surveys of 500 smallholder farmers, 30 key informant interviews, ecological field assessments, and laboratory analysis of pesticide residues in soil, water, and vegetables. Quantitative data were analyzed descriptively and inferentially, while biodiversity indices measured species richness; qualitative data were thematically analyzed to explore knowledge, institutional barriers, and perceptions. Results show that 87% of farmers rely solely on chemical pesticides, often applying high doses based on visual inspection rather than integrated thresholds. Pesticide residues were detected in 85% of vegetable and 80% of soil samples, with 28% exceeding national maximum residue limits. Ecological assessments revealed lower populations of pollinators and beneficial predators in high pesticide-use areas compared to fields managed under IPM or ecological agriculture. Only 13% of farmers received IPM training, and under 11% practiced it actively. Economic analysis indicated that IPM fields achieved similar yields but lower input costs, generating higher net income. Biodiversity was notably higher in diversified farms with hedgerows, polycultures, and ecological buffer zones.

DESPRESCRIÇÃO DE BENZODIAZEPÍNICOS NA ATENÇÃO PRIMÁRIA À SAÚDE: ESTRATÉGIAS DE RETIRADA GRADUAL, BARREIRAS ASSISTENCIAIS E DESFECHOS CLÍNICOS
abstractText: Introdução: Os benzodiazepínicos constituem uma classe de psicofármacos amplamente utilizada no tratamento de transtornos de ansiedade, insônia e outras condições clínicas específicas, devido aos seus efeitos ansiolíticos, sedativos, hipnóticos, anticonvulsivantes e miorrelaxantes. Embora apresentem benefícios terapêuticos em determinadas situações, a utilização prolongada pode favorecer o desenvolvimento de tolerância, dependência física e sintomas de abstinência, além de estar associada a eventos adversos como comprometimento cognitivo, quedas e prejuízos psicomotores, especialmente em pessoas idosas. Metodologia: Trata-se de uma revisão integrativa da literatura, de caráter descritivo, com abordagem qualitativa, desenvolvida com o objetivo de reunir, analisar e sintetizar as evidências científicas disponíveis acerca da desprescrição de benzodiazepínicos na Atenção Primária à Saúde (APS), com enfoque nas estratégias de retirada gradual, nas barreiras relacionadas aos pacientes, aos profissionais e à organização dos serviços de saúde, bem como nos desfechos clínicos associados à redução ou à interrupção desses medicamentos. Resultados: A análise dos estudos selecionados evidencia que a desprescrição de benzodiazepínicos na Atenção Primária à Saúde (APS) constitui um processo clínico complexo, influenciado não apenas pela escolha da estratégia de redução da dose, mas também pelas características individuais dos pacientes, pela atuação dos profissionais e pelas condições de organização dos serviços de saúde. De maneira geral, as publicações convergem quanto à necessidade de uma retirada planejada, individualizada e acompanhada, em oposição à interrupção abrupta e desassistida. Considerações Finais: A presente revisão integrativa evidencia que a desprescrição de benzodiazepínicos na Atenção Primária à Saúde constitui uma estratégia relevante para a promoção do uso racional de medicamentos e a redução dos riscos associados ao tratamento prolongado. Os estudos analisados convergem quanto à importância da retirada gradual, do acompanhamento clínico individualizado e da participação ativa do paciente nas decisões terapêuticas.

title: Linking Principals’ Digital Leadership to Teacher Performance through Digital Transformation Readiness: An Integrative Literature Review
abstractText: Digital transformation has reshaped educational practices and increased the need for school leadership that can support teachers in adapting to technology-driven changes. However, existing studies tend to examine principals’ digital leadership, teacher readiness, and teacher performance separately, leaving the mechanism connecting these constructs insufficiently integrated. This study aims to synthesize existing evidence on the relationships among principals’ digital leadership, teachers’ digital transformation readiness, and teacher performance, and to develop an integrative framework explaining the potential role of readiness in linking leadership with professional performance. An integrative literature review was conducted using a predefined corpus of 12 scholarly articles published between 2022 and 2026. The articles were examined through structured evidence extraction, evidence classification, conceptual harmonization, relational synthesis, and integrative thematic synthesis. The findings show relatively consistent evidence that principals’ digital leadership is positively associated with teacher performance, while complementary evidence indicates relationships between digital leadership and digital readiness and between readiness for change and teacher performance. The synthesis further identifies teacher digital transformation readiness as a multidimensional construct encompassing capability readiness, psychological readiness, and organizationally enabled readiness. Nevertheless, none of the reviewed studies directly tested the complete pathway linking principals’ digital leadership to teacher performance through digital transformation readiness. Therefore, this review proposes digital transformation readiness as a theoretically plausible explanatory mechanism rather than an empirically confirmed mediator. The resulting leadership–readiness–performance framework highlights that effective educational digital transformation depends on the interaction between supportive digital leadership, teachers’ preparedness for change, and enabling organizational conditions.

abstractText: Objective: To evaluate the clinical and procedural characteristic, efficacy and safety of catheter ablation of cardiac arrhythmias using a three-dimensional (3D) electro-anatomical mapping system without fluoroscopy at Hanoi Heart Hospital. Methods: This cross-sectional study with follow-up included 97 patients who underwent electrophysiological study and catheter ablation using a 3D electroanatomical mapping system without fluoroscopy at Hanoi Heart Hospital from January to December 2025. The treated arrhythmias included premature ventricular contractions (PVCs), atrioventricular nodal reentrant tachycardia (AVNRT), Wolff–Parkinson–White (WPW) syndrome, atrioventricular reentrant tachycardia (AVRT), atrial tachycardia (AT), and ventricular tachycardia (VT). Clinical characteristics, procedural duration, ablation time, procedural success, complications, and arrhythmia recurrence during follow-up were recorded. Results: The mean age was 47.0 ± 17.5 years, and 66.0% of patients were female. PVCs were the most common arrhythmia (53.6%), followed by AVNRT (22.7%) and WPW syndrome (12.5%). The mean procedure duration was 47.2 ± 12.1 minutes, while the mean ablation time was 266.0 ± 155.8 seconds. Overall procedural success was achieved in 96 of 97 patients (98.9%). No cases of cardiac tamponade, pneumothorax, coronary spasm, persistent complete atrioventricular block, or vascular complications at the access site were recorded. One patient developed transient atrioventricular block, which recovered spontaneously, and two patients experienced transient right bundle branch block. Five patients had model displacement (5,15%), necessitating re-mapping. During a median follow-up of 10 (7–13) months, two cases of arrhythmia recurrence were documented. Conclusion: Catheter ablation of cardiac arrhythmias using a 3D electroanatomical mapping system without fluoroscopy was feasible in selected patients, with a high procedural success rate and a low rate of complications. Pre-procedure preparation is crucial to avoid model displacement.

title: Left atrial functional characteristics using speckle tracking echocardiography in patients with non-valvular atrial fibrillation
abstractText: Objective: To investigate the functional characteristics of the left atrium using speckle tracking echocardiography in patients with non-valvular atrial fibrillation. Methods: A cross-sectional descriptive study was conducted on 46 patients with non-valvular atrial fibrillation and 33 control subjects without cardiovascular disease. All participants underwent evaluation for clinical symptoms, medical history, physical examination, electrocardiography, and echocardiography, including speckle tracking echocardiography to assess left atrial function. Results: From June 2023 to September 2025, 46 patients with non-valvular atrial fibrillation were enrolled in the study, alongside 33 control subjects with comparable age, BMI, and heart rate. The results demonstrated that patients with non-valvular atrial fibrillation had significantly reduced left atrial diameter on 2D, left atrial volume index (LAVi), reservoir function (LASr), conduit function (LAScd), and contraction function (LASct) compared to the control group (p < 0.001). No significant differences were observed in left atrial size and function among atrial fibrillation patients based on heart failure status. A trend toward lower LASr and LASct was observed in the atrial fibrillation patients who experienced stroke, howerver, the small number of stroke events limited the statistical power and precluded robust statistical comparisons. LAScd was decreased in atrial fibrillation patients aged 65 years. Conclusion: Left atrial reservoir, conduit, and contraction functions are all significantly reduced on speckle tracking echocardiography in patients with non-valvular atrial fibrillation.

title: Integrated Assessment Model for Quality and Safety Resources at A Textile Enterprise
abstractText: General Background Consistently maintaining product conformity and safety within fabric manufacturing requires the systematic, coordinated governance of personnel, raw materials, equipment, and tracking systems. Specific Background Although ISO 9001 frameworks and defect-control programs are widely utilized, manufacturing facilities traditionally monitor human, material, technological, and informational inputs through disparate and disconnected metrics rather than evaluating their combined systemic status. Knowledge Gap Current literature extensively covers quality governance frameworks and blockchain-based tracking; however, the integrated evaluation of these four interconnected operational dimensions into a single operationalized dynamic index remains unaddressed for fabric enterprises. Aims This study develops and applies a transparent dynamic framework integrating 27 condition proxies across 36 months of operational data to monitor enterprise health and prioritize administrative interventions. Results Utilizing expert-assigned weights for normalization and aggregation, the total overall score demonstrated a marked increase from 0.09 in the first month to 0.97 by month 36. This upward trend indicates measurable improvements across the targeted dimensions—human capital, material inputs, technical stability, and information tracking—providing clear operational, tactical, and strategic decision thresholds for administrators. Novelty This framework introduces a structured, single-metric monitoring scheme combining previously isolated categories, enabling rapid identification of specific operational weaknesses in fabric manufacturing. Implications Plant supervisors can utilize this dynamic index to swiftly detect input deficiencies and target specific interventions, though the metric serves as a systemic health proxy rather than a direct measure of actual product safety outcomes. Highlights: Integrating 27 initial operational metrics generates a unified dynamic index to monitor enterprise health and supply allocation. Over a 36-month observation period, the aggregated overall score rose from 0.09 to 0.97, reflecting broad systemic improvements. The integrated framework successfully pinpoints departmental weaknesses, enabling targeted operational, tactical, and strategic administrative responses. Keywords: Composite Indicator, Textile Enterprise, Resource Management, Traceability, Quality Management

title: The Effect of Road Geometric Conditions on Route Realignment of the Trans Papua Highway, Jayapura–Wamena Section, Mamberamo–Elelim Segment
abstractText: The Trans-Papua Highway is a vital transportation corridor connecting communities and improving regional accessibility in Papua, Indonesia. However, the Jayapura–Wamena section, particularly the Mamberamo–Elelim segment, crosses mountainous terrain with sharp horizontal curves, steep longitudinal grades, narrow road widths, and inadequate stopping sight distances. This study used a descriptive quantitative case study design to assess existing geometric conditions and determine the need for route realignment along a 41.3-km corridor from kilometer station 368+400 to 409+700. Existing horizontal and vertical alignments were evaluated against applicable geometric road design standards. Three route alternatives were compared using weighted multicriteria decision analysis. The results identified six critical road sections that failed to meet geometric design requirements. Eighteen horizontal curves had radii of 10–25 m, below the calculated minimum of 50.39 m. Longitudinal grades reached 10–15%, road widths ranged from 3 to 7 m, and available sight distances were approximately 20–30 m, below the required stopping sight distance of 45 m. The weighted evaluation ranked geometric-standard-based realignment first, scoring 5.00, followed by limited improvement at 3.00 and retention of the existing alignment at 1.45. The proposed realignment would reduce the combined length of the six critical sections from 15,498 m to 10,600 m, a reduction of 4,898 m or approximately 31.6%. These findings indicate that realignment is the preferred alternative based on the assessed geometric criteria, with potential benefits for alignment consistency, operational efficiency, and driving conditions along the corridor.

title: Explainable Artificial Intelligence for Designing Country-Specific Climate Mitigation and Sustainable Development Pathways
abstractText: This study compares six machine-learning models for predicting per-capita CO2 emissions in a panel of 118 countries over 2000–2020 and uses SHAP to examine the fitted XGBoost model. The test sample comprises 2019–2020. XGBoost achieved the lowest test RMSE (0.475) and highest R2 (0.324), indicating limited to moderate predictive fit. GDP per capita had the largest means absolute SHAP value (0.2821), followed by the country effect (0.0361). Renewable-energy associations differed across observations and should not be interpreted as a uniform emissions reduction. Country profiles and four descriptive clusters illustrate possible areas for policy review; SHAP contributions are predictive associations, not causal effects or evaluated policy impacts.

title: O ENSINO DE ÁLGEBRA NOS ANOS FINAIS DO ENSINO FUNDAMENTAL: DIFICULDADES DE APRENDIZAGEM NA TRANSIÇÃO DO PENSAMENTO ARITMÉTICO PARA O ALGÉBRICO
abstractText: Este artigo analisa as dificuldades de aprendizagem na transição do pensamento aritmético para o algébrico nos anos finais do Ensino Fundamental e discute possibilidades didáticas de superação. Desenvolveu-se uma pesquisa qualitativa, bibliográfica e analítico-propositiva, fundamentada em oito estudos brasileiros publicados entre 2021 e 2025. Os trabalhos investigados convergem ao identificar desafios relacionados à atribuição de significados às letras, à interpretação do sinal de igualdade, à generalização de padrões e à tradução de enunciados da linguagem verbal para a simbólica. Como experiência brasileira, examina-se uma sequência didática aplicada a estudantes do 9º ano em escola estadual de Manaus (AM), na qual o emprego de materiais concretos, resolução de problemas e atividades graduais favoreceu a construção de conceitos algébricos. Discute-se ainda oficina com 138 estudantes de Pernambuco, cuja análise destacou obstáculos de representação. Propõe-se uma trilha de aprendizagem em múltiplas representações, articulando padrões figurativos, tabelas, linguagem natural, expressões algébricas, tecnologias digitais e avaliação formativa de erros. Incluem-se atividades e representações originais, com dados expressamente didáticos, sem atribuição de resultados simulados às escolas investigadas. Conclui-se que a transição aritmética-algébrica exige mediação continuada e situações que privilegiem relações, generalização e argumentação em vez da simples manipulação de símbolos.

title: Numerical Solution of Optimal Feedback Control for Finite Horizon Optimal Control Problem with Growth Condition
abstractText: In this paper, we study approximation of optimal feedback control for the finite horizon optimal control problem with growth conditions for control systems and cost functionals. The optimal control problems with growth conditions are usually applied in practice. In reducing the boundedness for the dynamics function to the growth conditions, we have some difficulty in proving the convergence of the approximation scheme by the Euler scheme. First, we prove comparison principle of unbounded viscosity solution under the growth condition for the dynamics function and prove that the value function is the unique viscosity solution of the Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman (HJB) equation. We then construct a new approximation scheme using Euler implicit scheme for the finite horizon optimal control problem and prove that the approximation value function converges to the viscosity solution of the HJB equation as the discretization step goes to zero. Based on the approximations of the viscosity solution, we construct the optimal feedback controls for the corresponding discrete control systems. We consider an example to show the efficiency of the time-space approximation algorithm by the Euler implicit scheme through computational results.
